## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

- brandkit: Premium brand-kit image generation skill for creating high-end brand-guidelines boards, logo systems, identity decks, and visual-world presentations. Trained for minimalist, cinematic, editorial, dark-tech, luxury, cultural, security, gaming, developer-tool, and consumer-app brand systems. Optimized for intentional logo concepting, refined composition, sparse typography, strong symbolic meaning, premium mockups, art-directed imagery, and flexible grid layouts.
- claude-stack-doctor: Health-check Eric's automation/memory stack in one pass — launchd agents (com.keystone.morning, agysync, dailybackup, rituals, reconcile, adjudicate), Python venvs, memsearch, memory-compiler flush pipeline, backup freshness, and context budget — and diagnose what's silently broken. Use when the user says "/claude-stack-doctor", "stack doctor", "is my stack healthy", "did my scheduled jobs run", "check the memory pipeline", "why didn't the backup run", or when closeout/morning sessions should verify automation health.
- cli-hub-meta-skill: Discover agent-native CLIs for professional software. Access the live catalog to find tools for creative workflows, productivity, AI, and more.
- closeout: End-of-session sign-off ritual. Sweeps loose ends, commits and pushes what needs it, verifies memory capture, writes a cross-harness handoff, and reports "clear to sign off" or what's still open. Use when the user says "/closeout", "any loose ends?", "am I good to sign off?", "close out for the night", "closing out", "goodnight", "wrap up for the day", or asks for a system health check before leaving.
- code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- CreateSkill: Invoke BEFORE any skill work — creating, modifying, adding a workflow/tool to, renaming, validating, or canonicalizing any skill. Required by skills/CLAUDE.md; the single home for skill authoring in this workspace. Owns the skill lifecycle: scaffold (public TitleCase vs private _ALLCAPS, flat 2-level, Gotchas + Examples, BPE check), validate, canonicalize, test, improve, optimize descriptions. USE WHEN create skill, new skill, make a skill, build a skill, set up a skill, private skill, make a X skill, add a workflow, add a tool, edit/change/update/rename a skill, skill frontmatter, validate skill, check skill, canonicalize, scaffold skill, test skill, improve skill, optimize description, skill not triggering, overtriggering. - design-taste-frontend: Anti-slop frontend skill for landing pages, portfolios, and redesigns. The agent reads the brief, infers the right design direction, and ships interfaces that do not look templated. Real design systems when applicable, audit-first on redesigns, strict pre-flight check.
- design-taste-frontend-v1: The original v1 taste-skill, preserved for projects depending on its exact behavior. The current default is `design-taste-frontend` (v2 experimental), which is a substantial rewrite. Use this v1 install name only if you need exact backward compatibility.
- doctor-plus: Runs Claude Code's built-in /doctor health check, then audits the workspace against the 6 then-and-now context-engineering shifts Anthropic shipped with the Claude 5 models (rules to judgement, examples to interfaces, upfront to progressive disclosure, repeats to tool descriptions, CLAUDE.md memory to auto-memory, simple specs to rich references). Reports findings first, fixes only on approval. Triggers on "/doctor-plus", "doctor plus", "doctor-plus", "extended doctor", "then and now audit", "context checkup".
- fireflies-intake: One-command Fireflies pipeline — sync new meeting transcripts into the SecondBrain vault, rename generically-titled meetings, then report exactly what was ingested. Use when the user says "/fireflies-intake", "ingest my recent fireflies meetings", "sync meetings that aren't in the second brain yet", "pull in the new meetings", "meeting ingestion", or asks whether all recent meetings have been ingested.
- five-slides-generator: Generate a '5 Slides in 5 Minutes' PowerPoint deck for Baylor Athletics Applied Performance — research, narrative, pptxgenjs, .pptx build, QA. Use whenever the user mentions '5 slides,' '5 slides in 5 minutes,' or gives a topic they want a Performance School deck on. Also trigger for a cross-functional staff presentation, a quick sport science deck, or any short educational deck in the established series format (CMJ, GPS, VBT are prior examples).
- forecast-capture: Capture and freeze the CFB Victory Model's pre-game forecasts before kickoff, then report what moved since last week. Run every Wednesday during the season. # Athletics Technology Inventory — Form Build Spec

## Built — live Google Form (scaffold)

A working Google Form has been created from this spec, to be transformed into
Microsoft Forms.

- **Edit / view:** https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1qVAdjmDs0uNGz1pV-1Nzdb6sEHx7RxL6MQmZd1pHsks/edit
- **Preview as respondent:** https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfP3vLBN6RrdXPHit1NFAEEug7MnnQZhco3W6vVZO2Y2c2EJw/viewform
- **Form ID:** `1qVAdjmDs0uNGz1pV-1Nzdb6sEHx7RxL6MQmZd1pHsks`
- Built via `gws forms` on the **personal** Google account (eric.rash11@gmail.com),
  not Baylor. 17 questions across 4 sections, verified against this spec.

> **Loose end:** the form is currently published and accepting responses. Nothing is
> shared, so exposure is minimal, but it should not collect real responses on a
> personal account. Turn off "Accepting responses" in the Forms UI, or delete the form
> once it has been transformed to Microsoft Forms.

---

**Platform for actual collection: Microsoft Forms**, not Google Forms. Baylor is a Microsoft tenant (Teams,
OneDrive, SharePoint), responses stay inside Baylor, and results drop straight to
Excel on OneDrive. Collecting an inventory of athlete-data systems through a personal
Google account would work against the point of the exercise.

**Audience:** Directors of Operations, one response per sport program or unit.
Also usable as an in-person conversation script — same questions, someone else types.

**Design rule:** every question that asks for certainty offers **"Not sure."** Jon
Allen's estimate is that 80–90% of platforms are known and the rest surface as
surprises. Forcing certainty produces confident wrong answers instead of a usable
map of what nobody knows.

**Target completion time: under 10 minutes.**

---

## Section 1 — About you

1. **Your name** — short answer
2. **Sport or unit** — dropdown, 26 options
   *Sports:* Baseball · Basketball (M) · Basketball (W) · Football · Golf (M) ·
   Golf (W) · Soccer · Softball · Tennis (M) · Tennis (W) ·
   Track & Field / Cross Country · Volleyball · Acrobatics & Tumbling · Equestrian
   *Units:* Applied Performance · Athletics Performance · Athletic Medicine ·
   Athletic Mental Health Services · Performance Nutrition ·
   Student-Athlete Services · Business Office · Communications · Marketing ·
   Compliance · Operations · Other

---

## Section 2 — Technology currently in use

*Repeat this block for each item. In Microsoft Forms, either use a repeating section
or instruct "submit the form once per technology" — a single submission per item is
easier to analyze and easier to fill.*

3. **Name of the technology, software, app, or platform** — short answer
4. **What do you use it for?** — one or two sentences
5. **Who uses it?** — checkboxes, select all
   Coaches · Athletics Performance · Athletic Medicine · Operations ·
   Analytics / Video · Student-athletes themselves · Other
   *Renamed to match the unit names in Q2. Performance Nutrition, Applied
   Performance, and Athletic Mental Health Services are deliberately not listed here
   — this question captures broad user groups rather than the full org chart. Say the
   word if they should be added.*
6. **Does it involve any student-athlete information?** — choice
   Yes · No · Not sure
7. **If yes, what kind?** — checkboxes, select all
   Names or roster only · Video of athletes · Performance or training data ·
   Health, injury, or medical · Wellness or survey responses · Academic ·
   Not sure
8. **Roughly when did you start using it?** — choice
   Within the last year · 1–3 years ago · More than 3 years ago · Not sure
9. **How is it paid for?** — choice
   Sport program budget · Department budget · Free / no cost ·
   Provided by a vendor or partner · Not sure
10. **Do you know when the contract or subscription ends?** — short answer,
    "Not sure" allowed
11. **How was it originally set up — did it go through the ITS IDEA form?** — choice
    Yes, through the IDEA form · No, we set it up directly with the vendor ·
    It came with something else we already had · Not sure

> Question 11 is the one that turns an anecdote into a number. The meeting put the
> bypass rate at roughly 20% by estimate. This measures it.

---

## Section 3 — Technology you have stopped using

12. **Have you stopped using any technology or software in the last year or so?**
    — Yes / No. If No, skip to Section 4.
13. **What was it?** — short answer
14. **Why did you stop?** — choice
    Cost · Didn't get used · Replaced by something better · Staff change ·
    Vendor issue · Other
15. **Do you know whether the vendor still has our data?** — choice
    They deleted it · They still have it · We exported it first · Not sure

> Question 15 matters more than it looks. If a product was discontinued and the
> vendor still holds student-athlete data, that is an open exposure with no owner.
> Nothing in the current process closes that loop.

---

## Section 4 — Coming up

16. **Is there anything you are currently evaluating, or planning to request?**
    — long answer, optional
17. **Anything you use that you are not sure counts as "technology"?**
    — long answer, optional

> Question 17 catches the long tail — shared spreadsheets, a free scheduling app, a
> vendor portal, a phone app a coach installed. That tail is exactly the 10–20%
> nobody currently has visibility into.

---

## After collection

# Athletics Technology Inventory — Form Build Spec

## Built — live Google Form (scaffold)

A working Google Form has been created from this spec, to be transformed into
Microsoft Forms.

- **Edit / view:** https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1qVAdjmDs0uNGz1pV-1Nzdb6sEHx7RxL6MQmZd1pHsks/edit
- **Preview as respondent:** https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfP3vLBN6RrdXPHit1NFAEEug7MnnQZhco3W6vVZO2Y2c2EJw/viewform
- **Form ID:** `1qVAdjmDs0uNGz1pV-1Nzdb6sEHx7RxL6MQmZd1pHsks`
- Built via `gws forms` on the **personal** Google account (eric.rash11@gmail.com),
  not Baylor. 17 questions across 4 sections, verified against this spec.

> **Loose end:** the form is currently published and accepting responses. Nothing is
> shared, so exposure is minimal, but it should not collect real responses on a
> personal account. Turn off "Accepting responses" in the Forms UI, or delete the form
> once it has been transformed to Microsoft Forms.

---

**Platform for actual collection: Microsoft Forms**, not Google Forms. Baylor is a Microsoft tenant (Teams,
OneDrive, SharePoint), responses stay inside Baylor, and results drop straight to
Excel on OneDrive. Collecting an inventory of athlete-data systems through a personal
Google account would work against the point of the exercise.

**Audience:** Directors of Operations, one response per sport program or unit.
Also usable as an in-person conversation script — same questions, someone else types.

**Design rule:** every question that asks for certainty offers **"Not sure."** Jon
Allen's estimate is that 80–90% of platforms are known and the rest surface as
surprises. Forcing certainty produces confident wrong answers instead of a usable
map of what nobody knows.

**Target completion time: under 10 minutes.**

---

## Section 1 — About you

1. **Your name** — short answer
2. **Sport or unit** — dropdown, 26 options
   *Sports:* Baseball · Basketball (M) · Basketball (W) · Football · Golf (M) ·
   Golf (W) · Soccer · Softball · Tennis (M) · Tennis (W) ·
   Track & Field / Cross Country · Volleyball · Acrobatics & Tumbling · Equestrian
   *Units:* Applied Performance · Athletics Performance · Athletic Medicine ·
   Athletic Mental Health Services · Performance Nutrition ·
   Student-Athlete Services · Business Office · Communications · Marketing ·
   Compliance · Operations · Other

---

## Section 2 — Technology currently in use

*Repeat this block for each item. In Microsoft Forms, either use a repeating section
or instruct "submit the form once per technology" — a single submission per item is
easier to analyze and easier to fill.*

3. **Name of the technology, software, app, or platform** — short answer
4. **What do you use it for?** — one or two sentences
5. **Who uses it?** — checkboxes, select all
   Coaches · Athletics Performance · Athletic Medicine · Operations ·
   Analytics / Video · Student-athletes themselves · Other
   *Renamed to match the unit names in Q2. Performance Nutrition, Applied
   Performance, and Athletic Mental Health Services are deliberately not listed here
   — this question captures broad user groups rather than the full org chart. Say the
   word if they should be added.*
6. **Does it involve any student-athlete information?** — choice
   Yes · No · Not sure
7. **If yes, what kind?** — checkboxes, select all
   Names or roster only · Video of athletes · Performance or training data ·
   Health, injury, or medical · Wellness or survey responses · Academic ·
   Not sure
8. **Roughly when did you start using it?** — choice
   Within the last year · 1–3 years ago · More than 3 years ago · Not sure
9. **How is it paid for?** — choice
   Sport program budget · Department budget · Free / no cost ·
   Provided by a vendor or partner · Not sure
10. **Do you know when the contract or subscription ends?** — short answer,
    "Not sure" allowed
11. **How was it originally set up — did it go through the ITS IDEA form?** — choice
    Yes, through the IDEA form · No, we set it up directly with the vendor ·
    It came with something else we already had · Not sure

> Question 11 is the one that turns an anecdote into a number. The meeting put the
> bypass rate at roughly 20% by estimate. This measures it.

---

## Section 3 — Technology you have stopped using

12. **Have you stopped using any technology or software in the last year or so?**
    — Yes / No. If No, skip to Section 4.
13. **What was it?** — short answer
14. **Why did you stop?** — choice
    Cost · Didn't get used · Replaced by something better · Staff change ·
    Vendor issue · Other
15. **Do you know whether the vendor still has our data?** — choice
    They deleted it · They still have it · We exported it first · Not sure

> Question 15 matters more than it looks. If a product was discontinued and the
> vendor still holds student-athlete data, that is an open exposure with no owner.
> Nothing in the current process closes that loop.

---

## Section 4 — Coming up

16. **Is there anything you are currently evaluating, or planning to request?**
    — long answer, optional
17. **Anything you use that you are not sure counts as "technology"?**
    — long answer, optional

> Question 17 catches the long tail — shared spreadsheets, a free scheduling app, a
> vendor portal, a phone app a coach installed. That tail is exactly the 10–20%
> nobody currently has visibility into.

---

## After collection

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Clean the Athletics Technology Quick Inventory export into tidy CSVs.

Run:
    uv run --with openpyxl python3 scripts/clean_inventory.py

Input:  raw/Quick_Inventory_export_<date>.xlsx  (newest file wins)
Output: clean/*.csv

The parser is mechanical. Every judgement call lives in scripts/aliases.py.
Anything the alias map does not recognise lands in clean/unmapped_review.csv
instead of being silently guessed.
"""

import csv
import glob
import os
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from aliases import ALIAS, CATEGORY, ATHLETE_DATA_CATEGORIES, UNCERTAIN  # noqa: E402

import openpyxl  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
CLEAN = os.path.join(ROOT, "clean")

# The 26 dropdown options the form offered, per docs/INVENTORY_FORMS_LINKS.md.
EXPECTED_UNITS = [
    "Baseball", "Basketball (M)", "Basketball (W)", "Football", "Golf (M)",
    "Golf (W)", "Soccer", "Softball", "Tennis (M)", "Tennis (W)",
    "Track & Field / Cross Country", "Volleyball", "Acrobatics & Tumbling",
    "Equestrian", "Applied Performance", "Athletics Performance",
    "Athletic Medicine", "Athletic Mental Health Services",
    "Performance Nutrition", "Student-Athlete Services", "Business Office",
    "Communications", "Marketing", "Compliance", "Operations", "Other",
]

# Free-text unit answers that do not match the dropdown exactly.
UNIT_FIX = {
    "athletics communications": "Communications",
    "development": "Other (Development)",
    "athletic performance": "Athletics Performance",
}

PLANNED_HINTS = ("about to be installed", "not in use yet", "will receive",
                 "have not yet received", "not yet")

# A response that is prose, not a list. Flagged, never parsed into products.
PROSE_MIN_WORDS = 12


def norm_key(s):
    """Lowercase and strip punctuation so alias lookup is forgiving."""
    s = s.lower().strip()
    s = re.sub(r"[^\w\s&/-]", " ", s)
    s = re.sub(r"[-_/]", " ", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
    return s


def strip_qty(item):
    """'MacBook x11' -> ('MacBook', 11). 'iPad x over 10' -> ('iPad', 10)."""
    m = re.search(r"\s+x\s*(?:at least\s*|over\s*)?(\d+)\s*$", item, re.I)
    if m:
        return item[: m.start()].strip(), int(m.group(1))
    return item.strip(), 1


def split_items(text):
    """Split one free-text answer into candidate technology strings.

    Handles, in order:
      - newline-separated lists
      - '-' sub-bullets, which attach to the vendor on the line above
      - 'Vendor (A, B, C)'  -> Vendor A / Vendor B / Vendor C
      - 'Vendor - A, B, C'  -> Vendor A / Vendor B / Vendor C
      - plain comma lists
    Returns list of (raw_item, parent_vendor_or_None).
    """
    out = []
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in text.split("\n")]
    last_parent = None

    for line in lines:
        if not line:
            continue

        # sub-bullet: belongs to the vendor named on a previous line
        if line.startswith("-"):
            item = line.lstrip("- ").strip()
            if item:
                out.append((item, last_parent))
            continue

        # Vendor (A, B, C)
        m = re.match(r"^(.+?)\s*\((.+)\)\s*$", line)
        if m and "," in m.group(2):
            vendor, inner = m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2)
            last_parent = vendor
            for part in inner.split(","):
                part = part.strip()
                if part:
                    out.append((part, vendor))
            continue

        # Vendor - A, B, C
        m = re.match(r"^(.+?)\s+-\s+(.+)$", line)
        if m and "," in m.group(2):
            vendor, inner = m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2)
            last_parent = vendor
            for part in inner.split(","):
                part = part.strip()
                if part:
                    out.append((part, vendor))
            continue

        # plain comma list, or a single item
        if "," in line and not re.search(r"\(", line):
            for part in line.split(","):
                part = part.strip()
                if part:
                    out.append((part, None))
                    last_parent = part
        else:
            out.append((line, None))
            last_parent = line

    return out


def resolve(raw_item, parent):
    """Map a raw string to (canonical, category, how_resolved)."""
    base, _qty = strip_qty(raw_item)
    k = norm_key(base)

    if k in ALIAS:
        c = ALIAS[k]
        return c, CATEGORY.get(c, "uncategorised"), "alias"

    # try 'Parent Item' e.g. parent='Catapult', item='Vault'
    if parent:
        pk = norm_key(f"{parent} {base}")
        if pk in ALIAS:
            c = ALIAS[pk]
            return c, CATEGORY.get(c, "uncategorised"), "alias+parent"
        ppk = norm_key(parent)
        if k in ALIAS:
            c = ALIAS[k]
            return c, CATEGORY.get(c, "uncategorised"), "alias"
        if ppk in ALIAS:
            c = ALIAS[ppk]
            return c, CATEGORY.get(c, "uncategorised"), "parent-fallback"

    return None, None, "unmapped"


def main():
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "raw", "Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx")))
    if not files:
        sys.exit("No raw export found in raw/")
    src = files[-1]
    print(f"input: {os.path.basename(src)}")

    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(src, read_only=True)
    rows = list(wb.active.iter_rows(values_only=True))
    header, data = rows[0], [r for r in rows[1:] if any(c not in (None, "") for c in r)]

    C_NAME, C_ROLE, C_UNIT, C_USING, C_STOPPED = 5, 6, 7, 8, 9

    long_rows, unmapped, prose_flags, stopped_rows = [], [], [], []
    units_seen = []

    for i, r in enumerate(data, start=1):
        unit_raw = (r[C_UNIT] or "").strip()
        unit = UNIT_FIX.get(norm_key(unit_raw), unit_raw)
        role = (r[C_ROLE] or "").strip()
        units_seen.append(unit)

        using = (r[C_USING] or "").strip()
        if using:
            words = len(using.split())
            if words >= PROSE_MIN_WORDS and "\n" not in using and using.count(",") < 2:
                prose_flags.append({
                    "response_id": i, "unit": unit, "role": role,
                    "text": using,
                    "note": "Prose answer, not a technology list. Needs a follow-up.",
                })
                continue

            for raw_item, parent in split_items(using):
                base, qty = strip_qty(raw_item)
                canon, cat, how = resolve(raw_item, parent)
                status = "planned" if any(h in raw_item.lower() for h in PLANNED_HINTS) else "in_use"
                if canon is None:
                    unmapped.append({
                        "response_id": i, "unit": unit, "raw_item": base,
                        "parent": parent or "",
                        "note": "Not in aliases.py. Add a mapping or confirm it is real.",
                    })
                    canon, cat = base, "uncategorised"
                long_rows.append({
                    "response_id": i,
                    "unit": unit,
                    "role": role,
                    "raw_item": base,
                    "canonical": canon,
                    "category": cat,
                    "qty": qty,
                    "status": status,
                    "athlete_data_likely": "Y" if cat in ATHLETE_DATA_CATEGORIES else "N",
                    "resolved_by": how,
                })

        stopped = (r[C_STOPPED] or "").strip()
        if stopped and norm_key(stopped) not in ("n a", "na", "none", "no"):
            for raw_item, parent in split_items(stopped):
                base, _ = strip_qty(raw_item)
                canon, cat, how = resolve(raw_item, parent)
                stopped_rows.append({
                    "response_id": i, "unit": unit, "role": role,
                    "raw_item": base,
                    "canonical": canon or base,
                    "category": cat or "uncategorised",
                    "resolved_by": how,
                    "vendor_data_status": "UNKNOWN - not asked on Quick form",
                })

    os.makedirs(CLEAN, exist_ok=True)

    def write(name, rows_, fields):
        p = os.path.join(CLEAN, name)
        with open(p, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fields)
            w.writeheader()
            w.writerows(rows_)
        print(f"  wrote {name}: {len(rows_)} rows")

    write("tech_inventory_long.csv", long_rows,
          ["response_id", "unit", "role", "raw_item", "canonical", "category",
           "qty", "status", "athlete_data_likely", "resolved_by"])

    # master: one row per canonical technology
    master = {}
    for row in long_rows:
        c = row["canonical"]
        m = master.setdefault(c, {
            "canonical": c, "category": row["category"],
            "athlete_data_likely": row["athlete_data_likely"],
            "units": set(), "raw_variants": set(), "review_note": UNCERTAIN.get(c, ""),
        })
        m["units"].add(row["unit"])
        m["raw_variants"].add(row["raw_item"])
    master_rows = sorted(
        ({"canonical": m["canonical"], "category": m["category"],
          "athlete_data_likely": m["athlete_data_likely"],
          "unit_count": len(m["units"]),
          "units": "; ".join(sorted(m["units"])),
          "raw_variants": " | ".join(sorted(m["raw_variants"])),
          "review_note": m["review_note"]} for m in master.values()),
        key=lambda x: (-x["unit_count"], x["canonical"]),
    )
    write("tech_master.csv", master_rows,
          ["canonical", "category", "athlete_data_likely", "unit_count",
           "units", "raw_variants", "review_note"])

    # coverage: who answered, who did not, who answered twice
    counts = {}
    for u in units_seen:
        counts[u] = counts.get(u, 0) + 1
    cov = []
    for u in EXPECTED_UNITS:
        cov.append({"unit": u, "responses": counts.get(u, 0),
                    "status": "responded" if counts.get(u, 0) == 1
                    else ("MULTIPLE" if counts.get(u, 0) > 1 else "NO RESPONSE")})
    for u, n in counts.items():
        if u not in EXPECTED_UNITS:
            cov.append({"unit": u, "responses": n, "status": "OFF-LIST ANSWER"})
    write("coverage.csv", cov, ["unit", "responses", "status"])

    write("stopped_using.csv", stopped_rows,
          ["response_id", "unit", "role", "raw_item", "canonical", "category",
           "resolved_by", "vendor_data_status"])
    write("unmapped_review.csv", unmapped,
          ["response_id", "unit", "raw_item", "parent", "note"])
    write("prose_responses_review.csv", prose_flags,
          ["response_id", "unit", "role", "text", "note"])

    print(f"\nresponses: {len(data)}")
    print(f"technology mentions: {len(long_rows)}")
    print(f"distinct technologies: {len(master_rows)}")
    print(f"unmapped needing review: {len(unmapped)}")
    print(f"units with no response: {sum(1 for c in cov if c['status'] == 'NO RESPONSE')}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

            item = line.lstrip("- ").strip()
            if item:
                out.append((item, last_parent))
            continue

        # Vendor (A, B, C)
        m = re.match(r"^(.+?)\s*\((.+)\)\s*$", line)
        if m and "," in m.group(2):
            vendor, inner = m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2)
            last_parent = vendor
            for part in inner.split(","):
                part = part.strip()
                if part:
                    out.append((part, vendor))
            continue

        # Vendor - A, B, C
        m = re.match(r"^(.+?)\s+-\s+(.+)$", line)
        if m and "," in m.group(2):
            vendor, inner = m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2)
            last_parent = vendor
            for part in inner.split(","):
                part = part.strip()
                if part:
                    out.append((part, vendor))
            continue

        # plain comma list, or a single item
        if "," in line and not re.search(r"\(", line):
            for part in line.split(","):
                part = part.strip()
                if part:
                    out.append((part, None))
                    last_parent = part
        else:
            out.append((line, None))
            last_parent = line

    return out


def resolve(raw_item, parent):
    """Map a raw string to (canonical, category, how_resolved)."""
    base, _qty = strip_qty(raw_item)
    k = norm_key(base)

    if k in ALIAS:
        c = ALIAS[k]
        return c, CATEGORY.get(c, "uncategorised"), "alias"

    # try 'Parent Item' e.g. parent='Catapult', item='Vault'
    if parent:
        pk = norm_key(f"{parent} {base}")
        if pk in ALIAS:
            c = ALIAS[pk]
            return c, CATEGORY.get(c, "uncategorised"), "alias+parent"
        ppk = norm_key(parent)
        if k in ALIAS:
            c = ALIAS[k]
            return c, CATEGORY.get(c, "uncategorised"), "alias"
        if ppk in ALIAS:
            c = ALIAS[ppk]
            return c, CATEGORY.get(c, "uncategorised"), "parent-fallback"

    return None, None, "unmapped"


def main():
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "raw", "Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx")))
    if not files:
        sys.exit("No raw export found in raw/")
    src = files[-1]
    print(f"input: {os.path.basename(src)}")

    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(src, read_only=True)
    rows = list(wb.active.iter_rows(values_only=True))
    header, data = rows[0], [r for r in rows[1:] if any(c not in (None, "") for c in r)]

    C_NAME, C_ROLE, C_UNIT, C_USING, C_STOPPED = 5, 6, 7, 8, 9

    long_rows, unmapped, prose_flags, stopped_rows = [], [], [], []
    units_seen = []

    for i, r in enumerate(data, start=1):
        unit_raw = (r[C_UNIT] or "").strip()
        unit = UNIT_FIX.get(norm_key(unit_raw), unit_raw)
        role = (r[C_ROLE] or "").strip()
        units_seen.append(unit)

        using = (r[C_USING] or "").strip()
        if using:
            words = len(using.split())
            if words >= PROSE_MIN_WORDS and "\n" not in using and using.count(",") < 2:
                prose_flags.append({
                    "response_id": i, "unit": unit, "role": role,
                    "text": using,
                    "note": "Prose answer, not a technology list. Needs a follow-up.",
                })
                continue

            for raw_item, parent in split_items(using):
                base, qty = strip_qty(raw_item)
                canon, cat, how = resolve(raw_item, parent)
                status = "planned" if any(h in raw_item.lower() for h in PLANNED_HINTS) else "in_use"
                if canon is None:
                    unmapped.append({
                        "response_id": i, "unit": unit, "raw_item": base,
                        "parent": parent or "",
                        "note": "Not in aliases.py. Add a mapping or confirm it is real.",
                    })
                    canon, cat = base, "uncategorised"
                long_rows.append({
                    "response_id": i,
                    "unit": unit,
                    "role": role,
                    "raw_item": base,
                    "canonical": canon,
                    "category": cat,
                    "qty": qty,
                    "status": status,
                    "athlete_data_likely": "Y" if cat in ATHLETE_DATA_CATEGORIES else "N",
                    "resolved_by": how,
                })

        stopped = (r[C_STOPPED] or "").strip()
        if stopped and norm_key(stopped) not in ("n a", "na", "none", "no"):
            for raw_item, parent in split_items(stopped):
                base, _ = strip_qty(raw_item)
                canon, cat, how = resolve(raw_item, parent)
                stopped_rows.append({
                    "response_id": i, "unit": unit, "role": role,
                    "raw_item": base,
                    "canonical": canon or base,
                    "category": cat or "uncategorised",
                    "resolved_by": how,
                    "vendor_data_status": "UNKNOWN - not asked on Quick form",
                })

    os.makedirs(CLEAN, exist_ok=True)

    def write(name, rows_, fields):
        p = os.path.join(CLEAN, name)
        with open(p, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fields)
            w.writeheader()
            w.writerows(rows_)
        print(f"  wrote {name}: {len(rows_)} rows")

    write("tech_inventory_long.csv", long_rows,
          ["response_id", "unit", "role", "raw_item", "canonical", "category",
           "qty", "status", "athlete_data_likely", "resolved_by"])

    # master: one row per canonical technology
    master = {}
    for row in long_rows:
        c = row["canonical"]
        m = master.setdefault(c, {
            "canonical": c, "category": row["category"],
            "athlete_data_likely": row["athlete_data_likely"],
            "units": set(), "raw_variants": set(), "review_note": UNCERTAIN.get(c, ""),
        })
        m["units"].add(row["unit"])
        m["raw_variants"].add(row["raw_item"])
    master_rows = sorted(
        ({"canonical": m["canonical"], "category": m["category"],
          "athlete_data_likely": m["athlete_data_likely"],
          "unit_count": len(m["units"]),
          "units": "; ".join(sorted(m["units"])),
          "raw_variants": " | ".join(sorted(m["raw_variants"])),
          "review_note": m["review_note"]} for m in master.values()),
        key=lambda x: (-x["unit_count"], x["canonical"]),
    )
    write("tech_master.csv", master_rows,
          ["canonical", "category", "athlete_data_likely", "unit_count",
           "units", "raw_variants", "review_note"])

    # coverage: who answered, who did not, who answered twice
    counts = {}
    for u in units_seen:
        counts[u] = counts.get(u, 0) + 1
    cov = []
    for u in EXPECTED_UNITS:
        cov.append({"unit": u, "responses": counts.get(u, 0),
                    "status": "responded" if counts.get(u, 0) == 1
                    else ("MULTIPLE" if counts.get(u, 0) > 1 else "NO RESPONSE")})
    for u, n in counts.items():
        if u not in EXPECTED_UNITS:
            cov.append({"unit": u, "responses": n, "status": "OFF-LIST ANSWER"})
    write("coverage.csv", cov, ["unit", "responses", "status"])

    write("stopped_using.csv", stopped_rows,
          ["response_id", "unit", "role", "raw_item", "canonical", "category",
           "resolved_by", "vendor_data_status"])
    write("unmapped_review.csv", unmapped,
          ["response_id", "unit", "raw_item", "parent", "note"])
    write("prose_responses_review.csv", prose_flags,
          ["response_id", "unit", "role", "text", "note"])

    print(f"\nresponses: {len(data)}")
    print(f"technology mentions: {len(long_rows)}")
    print(f"distinct technologies: {len(master_rows)}")
    print(f"unmapped needing review: {len(unmapped)}")
    print(f"units with no response: {sum(1 for c in cov if c['status'] == 'NO RESPONSE')}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Clean the Athletics Technology Quick Inventory export into tidy CSVs.
3	
4	Run:
5	    uv run --with openpyxl python3 scripts/clean_inventory.py
6	
7	Input:  raw/Quick_Inventory_export_<date>.xlsx  (newest file wins)
8	Output: clean/*.csv
9	
10	The parser is mechanical. Every judgement call lives in scripts/aliases.py.
11	Anything the alias map does not recognise lands in clean/unmapped_review.csv
12	instead of being silently guessed.
13	"""
14	
15	import csv
16	import glob
17	import os
18	import re
19	import sys
20	
21	sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
22	from aliases import ALIAS, CATEGORY, ATHLETE_DATA_CATEGORIES, UNCERTAIN  # noqa: E402
23	
24	import openpyxl  # noqa: E402
25	
26	ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
27	CLEAN = os.path.join(ROOT, "clean")
28	
29	# The 26 dropdown options the form offered, per docs/INVENTORY_FORMS_LINKS.md.
30	EXPECTED_UNITS = [
31	    "Baseball", "Basketball (M)", "Basketball (W)", "Football", "Golf (M)",
32	    "Golf (W)", "Soccer", "Softball", "Tennis (M)", "Tennis (W)",
33	    "Track & Field / Cross Country", "Volleyball", "Acrobatics & Tumbling",
34	    "Equestrian", "Applied Performance", "Athletics Performance",
35	    "Athletic Medicine", "Athletic Mental Health Services",
36	    "Performance Nutrition", "Student-Athlete Services", "Business Office",
37	    "Communications", "Marketing", "Compliance", "Operations", "Other",
38	]
39	
40	# Free-text unit answers that do not match the dropdown exactly.
41	UNIT_FIX = {
42	    "athletics communications": "Communications",
43	    "development": "Other (Development)",
44	    "athletic performance": "Athletics Performance",
45	}
46	
47	PLANNED_HINTS = ("about to be installed", "not in use yet", "will receive",
48	                 "have not yet received", "not yet")
49	
50	# A response that is prose, not a list. Flagged, never parsed into products.
51	PROSE_MIN_WORDS = 12
52	
53	
54	def norm_key(s):
55	    """Lowercase and strip punctuation so alias lookup is forgiving."""
56	    s = s.lower().strip()
57	    s = re.sub(r"[^\w\s&/-]", " ", s)
58	    s = re.sub(r"[-_/]", " ", s)
59	    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
60	    return s
61	
62	
63	def strip_qty(item):
64	    """'MacBook x11' -> ('MacBook', 11). 'iPad x over 10' -> ('iPad', 10)."""
65	    m = re.search(r"\s+x\s*(?:at least\s*|over\s*)?(\d+)\s*$", item, re.I)
66	    if m:
67	        return item[: m.start()].strip(), int(m.group(1))
68	    return item.strip(), 1
69	
70	
71	def split_items(text):
72	    """Split one free-text answer into candidate technology strings.
73	
74	    Handles, in order:
75	      - newline-separated lists
76	      - '-' sub-bullets, which attach to the vendor on the line above
77	      - 'Vendor (A, B, C)'  -> Vendor A / Vendor B / Vendor C
78	      - 'Vendor - A, B, C'  -> Vendor A / Vendor B / Vendor C
79	      - plain comma lists
80	    Returns list of (raw_item, parent_vendor_or_None).
81	    """
82	    out = []
83	    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in text.split("\n")]
84	    last_parent = None
85	
86	    for line in lines:
87	        if not line:
88	            continue
89	
90	        # sub-bullet: belongs to the vendor named on a previous line
91	        if line.startswith("-"):
92	            item = line.lstrip("- ").strip()
93	            if item:
94	                out.append((item, last_parent))
95	            continue
96	
97	        # Vendor (A, B, C)
98	        m = re.match(r"^(.+?)\s*\((.+)\)\s*$", line)
99	        if m and "," in m.group(2):
100	            vendor, inner = m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2)
101	            last_parent = vendor
102	            for part in inner.split(","):
103	                part = part.strip()
104	                if part:
105	                    out.append((part, vendor))
106	            continue
107	
108	        # Vendor - A, B, C
109	        m = re.match(r"^(.+?)\s+-\s+(.+)$", line)
110	        if m and "," in m.group(2):
111	            vendor, inner = m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2)
112	            last_parent = vendor
113	            for part in inner.split(","):
114	                part = part.strip()
115	                if part:
116	                    out.append((part, vendor))
117	            continue
118	
119	        # slash list of single words: 'Claude/ChatGPT/FanWord'
120	        if "/" in line and "," not in line:
121	            parts = [p.strip() for p in line.split("/")]
122	            if len(parts) > 1 and all(p and " " not in p for p in parts):
123	                for p in parts:
124	                    out.append((p, None))
125	                last_parent = parts[-1]
126	                continue
127	
128	        # plain comma list, or a single item
129	        if "," in line and not re.search(r"\(", line):
130	            for part in line.split(","):
131	                part = part.strip()
132	                if part:
133	                    out.append((part, None))
134	                    last_parent = part
135	        else:
136	            out.append((line, None))
137	            last_parent = line
138	
139	    return out
140	
141	
142	def strip_notes(item):
143	    """Drop respondent asides so the product name is left.
144	
145	    'First Beat (not in use yet)' -> 'First Beat'
146	    'Track Man is about to be installed' -> 'Track Man'
147	    """
148	    item = re.sub(r"\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$", "", item).strip()
149	    item = re.split(r"\s+is about to be\b|\s+will be\b", item, flags=re.I)[0]
150	    return item.strip(" .,")
151	
152	
153	def resolve(raw_item, parent):
154	    """Map a raw string to (canonical, category, how_resolved)."""
155	    base, _qty = strip_qty(raw_item)
156	    base = strip_notes(base)
157	    k = norm_key(base)
158	
159	    if k in ALIAS:
160	        c = ALIAS[k]
161	        return c, CATEGORY.get(c, "uncategorised"), "alias"
162	
163	    # try 'Parent Item' e.g. parent='Catapult', item='Vault'
164	    if parent:
165	        pk = norm_key(f"{parent} {base}")
166	        if pk in ALIAS:
167	            c = ALIAS[pk]
168	            return c, CATEGORY.get(c, "uncategorised"), "alias+parent"
169	        ppk = norm_key(parent)
170	        if k in ALIAS:
171	            c = ALIAS[k]
172	            return c, CATEGORY.get(c, "uncategorised"), "alias"
173	        if ppk in ALIAS:
174	            c = ALIAS[ppk]
175	            return c, CATEGORY.get(c, "uncategorised"), "parent-fallback"
176	
177	    return None, None, "unmapped"
178	
179	
180	def main():
181	    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "raw", "Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx")))
182	    if not files:
183	        sys.exit("No raw export found in raw/")
184	    src = files[-1]
185	    print(f"input: {os.path.basename(src)}")

205	            if words >= PROSE_MIN_WORDS and "\n" not in using and using.count(",") < 2:
206	                prose_flags.append({
207	                    "response_id": i, "unit": unit, "role": role,
208	                    "text": using,

210	                })
211	                continue
212	
213	            for raw_item, parent in split_items(using):
214	                base, qty = strip_qty(raw_item)
215	                base = strip_notes(base)
216	                canon, cat, how = resolve(raw_item, parent)

Business Office — the unit holding the contract records the spec wanted to
cross-check against.

Three units submitted twice (Football, Athletic Medicine, Communications). The spec
asked for one response per unit. These are not duplicates of each other — they are
different people describing different slices of the same unit, so they were kept and
tagged, not merged.

parsed as technology.

- **40 of 83 (48%) plausibly touch student-athlete information** — performance,

  across two or more units.

| Category | Count |
|---|---|
| video-analytics | 15 |
| comms-media | 15 |
| performance | 12 |
| admin | 10 |
| medical | 6 |
| office-general | 5 |
| hardware | 5 |
| equipment-ops | 5 |
| academic | 5 |
| athlete-management | 2 |
| ai-general | 2 |
| facility | 1 |

Four vendors sell overlapping capability and all four are in the building:

| Vendor | Units | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Teamworks | 6 | Applied Performance, Baseball, Basketball (M), Compliance, Football, Student-Athlete Services |
| VALD | 5 | Applied Performance, Athletic Medicine, Athletics Performance, Basketball (M), Basketball (W) |
| Catapult | 4 | Applied Performance, Athletics Performance, Communications, Football |
| Kitman Labs | 4 | Applied Performance, Athletic Medicine, Athletics Performance, Basketball (M) |
| Kinexon | 3 | Athletics Performance, Basketball (M), Basketball (W) |
| Perch | 3 | Applied Performance, Athletics Performance, Basketball (W) |

Athlete tracking alone runs on **Catapult, Kinexon, Polar and Firstbeat** across
different programs. Force testing runs on **VALD, Perch, GymAware and TMG**. This is
a consolidation question, and it is answerable with 11 units — it will only sharpen
with 26.

---

## 4. Polar is listed as both stopped and active

- **Athletics Performance** stopped using Polar Team Pro.
- **Basketball (W)** stopped using Polar Team Pro.
- **Basketball (M)** lists Polar as currently in use.

Two units retired a product a third still runs. Nothing in the current process
notices this. Whether the retired units' athlete data was deleted, exported, or is
still sitting with the vendor is **not answerable from this form** — the Quick form
never asked. That is exactly the gap Q15 of the Detailed form was written to close.

---

## 5. Stopped in the last 12 months

| Unit | Product | Vendor still holds data? |
|---|---|---|
| Athletics Performance | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Basketball (W) | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Communications | StatCrew | Not asked |
| Softball | YakkerTech | Not asked |

Four confirmed retirements, **zero known data dispositions**. Every one is an open
exposure with no owner.

---

## 6. Coming online

- **Athletics Performance** — Firstbeat, purchased, not yet in use.
- **Softball** — Trackman, about to be installed.

Neither appears to have gone through a documented vetting step. The Quick form did
not ask about the ITS IDEA form, so this cannot be confirmed here.

The Quick form has 5 questions. These questions from the Detailed (17-question) form

- Does the vendor still hold data from discontinued products? (Q15)

The `athlete_data_likely` column in `clean/tech_master.csv` is **my category
inference, not a respondent answer.** Treat it as a screening list, not a finding.

---

## Recommended next steps

1. **Re-export from Microsoft Forms** and re-run the pipeline. Current numbers are

5. **Cross-check against Business Office contract records.**
   `~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-BaylorUniversity/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/99_UNSORTED/From_Desktop/Tech Expenses.xlsx`

# Tech_Inventory_Analysis

Cleaning and analysis of the Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory survey.

Companion to `~/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework`, which holds the framework
documents, the form specs, and the form links. This folder holds only the
collected data and what comes out of it.

## Layout

```
raw/     frozen survey exports, date-stamped. never edited.
scripts/ clean_inventory.py (parser) + aliases.py (all judgement calls)
clean/   generated CSVs. delete and regenerate freely.
docs/    findings
deliverables/  anything that goes to Kenny / Jon Allen / ITS
```

## Run

```bash
cd ~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis
uv run --with openpyxl python3 scripts/clean_inventory.py
```

The script reads the newest `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx` and rewrites
everything in `clean/`. It is safe to run repeatedly.

## Refresh with a newer export

1. Download the responses from Microsoft Forms.
2. Save as `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx`.
3. Re-run the command above.
4. Check `clean/unmapped_review.csv`. If it has rows, add them to
   `scripts/aliases.py` and run again. It should end empty.

## Outputs

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `clean/tech_inventory_long.csv` | one row per unit × technology |
| `clean/tech_master.csv` | one row per distinct technology, with unit count |
| `clean/coverage.csv` | which of the 26 units responded, missed, or answered twice |
| `clean/stopped_using.csv` | technology retired in the last 12 months |
| `clean/unmapped_review.csv` | strings the alias map did not recognise |
| `clean/prose_responses_review.csv` | answers that were prose, not a list |

## Ground rules

- **Nothing is guessed silently.** Unrecognised names go to
  `unmapped_review.csv` rather than being auto-matched.
- **All name merging lives in `scripts/aliases.py`.** The parser is mechanical.
- `raw/` is never modified. Re-analysis always starts from the frozen export.
- The export carries respondent names and email addresses. Strip those before
  anything is shared or published.

## Status

First pass done against the **2026-08-24** export: 15 responses, 11 units,
83 distinct technologies. See `docs/FINDINGS_2026-08-29.md`.

Provisional — the submission deadline fell after that export date. Re-export
and re-run before reporting numbers.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/project

# /project — portfolio registry skill

Drives the shipped `project-triage` CLI to capture ideas, log progress, and
keep the front-burner dashboard current. The registry (`portfolio.json`) is
the single source of truth — never hand-edit `dashboard.html`.

## Paths

- Repo: `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage`
- Interpreter: `python3`
- Registry: `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.json`
- CLI entry points: `portfolio.py` (mutations), `render.py` (render)
- Generated: `dashboard.html`, `pulse.md` (both written next to the scripts;
  do not edit by hand, they are regenerated every render)

## CLI contract (verbatim — do not alter flags)

```
& "python3" "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py" add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<source>"
& "python3" "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py" add-update "<name>" "<note>" --next-action "<optional>"
& "python3" "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py" set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"
& "python3" "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/render.py"
& "python3" "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/render.py" --no-scan
```

- `add-idea` prints `idea captured (<N> in inbox)`.
- `add-update` prints `updated <name>` (name match is case-insensitive).
- `set-stage` prints `stage set: <name> → <stage>`. Valid stages, in ladder
  order: `idea grilled spec planned building shipped`.
- `render.py` (full scan) prints `wrote dashboard.html · wrote pulse.md · ...`.
- `render.py --no-scan` does the same but skips the DEV/ activity heuristics
  (fast; use it after any registry mutation, and to validate hand-edits).
- Any error path prints `[error] <msg>` to stderr and exits 2, with no
  mutation to `portfolio.json`. Stop and surface the message verbatim.

## Verbs

### `idea <pitch>`
Run `add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<conversation context, ≤8 words>"`. The
source should summarize where the idea came from (e.g. "chat about GPS
vendor gaps"), not just "chat". Then do the render + republish ritual.

### `update <name> <note>`
Fuzzy-match `<name>` against the project names currently in the registry
(read `portfolio.json` first). If exactly one match, run `add-update "<name>"
"<note>"` (add `--next-action "<...>"` if the user gave one). If the match is
ambiguous or there's no close match, ask the user which project they mean
before running anything. Then do the render + republish ritual.

### `rank`
Read `portfolio.json`, show both lanes' active projects with their current
`rank` values, and ask for the new order. Never reorder ranks yourself —
only apply the order the user gives you. Rewrite the `rank` fields directly
with the Edit tool, then validate by running `render.py --no-scan` (exit 0
means the edit is structurally valid). Then do the render + republish
ritual (this counts as the render step — no need to run render.py twice).

### `promote <idea>`
Ask which lane (`job` or `side`) and for a `next_action`. With the Edit
tool: set the matching idea's `status` to `promoted`, and append a new
project entry to that lane at the next free `rank` (max existing rank in
that lane + 1). Validate with `render.py --no-scan`, then do the render +
republish ritual.

### `stage <name> <stage>`
Fuzzy-match `<name>` like `update` does. Run `set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"`.
The dashboard auto-detects spec/plan docs (in the project's DEV folder under
`docs/specs`, `docs/plans`, or the `docs/superpowers/...` variants) and
renders plan-checkbox progress — the stage is your curated claim; drift
between the two shows on the card. Then do the render + republish ritual.

**Shipped → harvest handoff:** when the stage being set is `shipped`, after
the ritual offer once: "Want me to run /harvest on <name> to distill it into
your SecondBrain and log the shipped artifact?" On yes, invoke the `harvest`
skill for that project.

### bare `/project`
Do the render + republish ritual, then show the contents of `pulse.md` in
chat.

## Render + republish ritual (run after every mutation)

1. Run `render.py --no-scan` (fast path — the mutation verbs above already
   changed the registry; a full DEV/ scan isn't needed unless the user
   explicitly asks for a fresh scan).
2. Read `meta.artifact_url` from `portfolio.json`.
   - If non-empty: publish `dashboard.html` via the Artifact tool passing
     `url: <meta.artifact_url>`, `favicon: "🔥"`, `title: "Portfolio — Front
     Burner"`.
   - If empty: publish `dashboard.html` via the Artifact tool with
     `favicon: "🔥"`, `title: "Portfolio — Front Burner"` (no `url`). Take
     the returned URL, write it into `meta.artifact_url` with the Edit tool,
     then re-run `render.py --no-scan` and republish once more (now with
     `url` set) so the rendered page displays its own share URL.

## Rules

- Never reorder project ranks yourself — only apply the order the user
  gives you during `rank`.
- Never delete a project or idea without explicit confirmation.
- On any `[error] ...` output from the CLI: stop immediately, show the
  error verbatim, and do not proceed to render/publish.

content.text:
Good question — I was not told. I found it and then proved it was the right file.

**How I found it**
1. Searched your memory for "technology inventory survey". Hit meeting notes about a tech inventory and a Microsoft Form.
2. Listed `~/DEV` → found `SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework`.
3. Read `docs/INVENTORY_FORM_SPEC_2026-08-13.md` and `docs/INVENTORY_FORMS_LINKS.md`. Those say: collect in **Microsoft Forms**, results land in **Excel on OneDrive**.
4. Checked your mounts → `OneDrive-BaylorUniversity` is mounted locally.
5. Searched that mount for spreadsheets with tech/survey/inventory in the name → one hit at the OneDrive root.

**How I proved it**
I opened the header row. The 5 columns match the Quick Inventory form spec word for word: Your Name, Your Role, Sport or Unit, "What technology and software is your department currently using", "Has your department stopped using any technology in the past 12 months?". Plus the Microsoft Forms system columns (Id, Start time, Completion time, Email, Name). That is the Quick form, not the Detailed one.

Path: `~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-BaylorUniversity/Athletics Technology - Quick Inventory.xlsx`

I copied it into the project as a frozen snapshot so re-runs never depend on the OneDrive mount.

Finishing the registry entry now.

# Athletics Technology Inventory — First-Pass Findings

**Date:** 2026-08-29
**Source:** `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_2026-08-24.xlsx` (Microsoft Forms, Quick Inventory, 5 questions)
**Pipeline:** `scripts/clean_inventory.py` + `scripts/aliases.py` → `clean/*.csv`

> **Provisional.** The local export was written **2026-08-24**. The submission
> deadline landed after that. Re-export from Microsoft Forms and re-run before any
> of these numbers go in front of Kenny, Jon Allen, or ITS. The pipeline is
> re-runnable: drop a newer `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_<date>.xlsx` in and run the
> script again.

---

## 1. Coverage is the headline, not the technology count

15 submissions. After removing one prose answer that listed no technology, **14
usable responses from 11 distinct units**.

The form offered 26 sport/unit options. **15 of them returned nothing:**

Golf (M) · Golf (W) · Soccer · Tennis (M) · Tennis (W) ·
Track & Field / Cross Country · Volleyball · Acrobatics & Tumbling · Equestrian ·
Athletic Mental Health Services · Performance Nutrition · Business Office ·
Marketing · Operations

**Every Olympic sport except Baseball, Basketball and Softball is missing.** So is
Business Office — the unit holding the contract records the spec wanted to
cross-check against.

Three units submitted twice (Football, Athletic Medicine, Communications). The spec
asked for one response per unit. These are not duplicates of each other — they are
different people describing different slices of the same unit, so they were kept and
tagged, not merged.

One answer came in off the dropdown list: **Development** (a new hire who has not yet
received a laptop or phone). Recorded in `clean/prose_responses_review.csv`, not
parsed as technology.

**Read this as: the inventory is roughly 42% complete by unit.**

---

## 2. What the responding units reported

- **155 technology mentions**, resolving to **83 distinct products**.
- **40 of 83 (48%) plausibly touch student-athlete information** — performance,
  medical, athlete-management, video-analytics, or academic.
- **66 of 83 (80%) were named by exactly one unit.** Only 17 products are shared
  across two or more units.

By category (distinct products):

| Category | Count |
|---|---|
| video-analytics | 15 |
| comms-media | 15 |
| performance | 12 |
| admin | 10 |
| medical | 6 |
| office-general | 5 |
| hardware | 5 |
| equipment-ops | 5 |
| academic | 5 |
| athlete-management | 2 |
| ai-general | 2 |
| facility | 1 |

---

## 3. Overlapping athlete-monitoring vendors

Four vendors sell overlapping capability and all four are in the building:

| Vendor | Units | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Teamworks | 6 | Applied Performance, Baseball, Basketball (M), Compliance, Football, Student-Athlete Services |
| VALD | 5 | Applied Performance, Athletic Medicine, Athletics Performance, Basketball (M), Basketball (W) |
| Catapult | 4 | Applied Performance, Athletics Performance, Communications, Football |
| Kitman Labs | 4 | Applied Performance, Athletic Medicine, Athletics Performance, Basketball (M) |
| Kinexon | 3 | Athletics Performance, Basketball (M), Basketball (W) |
| Perch | 3 | Applied Performance, Athletics Performance, Basketball (W) |

Athlete tracking alone runs on **Catapult, Kinexon, Polar and Firstbeat** across
different programs. Force testing runs on **VALD, Perch, GymAware and TMG**. This is
a consolidation question, and it is answerable with 11 units — it will only sharpen
with 26.

---

## 4. Polar is listed as both stopped and active

- **Athletics Performance** stopped using Polar Team Pro.
- **Basketball (W)** stopped using Polar Team Pro.
- **Basketball (M)** lists Polar as currently in use.

Two units retired a product a third still runs. Nothing in the current process
notices this. Whether the retired units' athlete data was deleted, exported, or is
still sitting with the vendor is **not answerable from this form** — the Quick form
never asked. That is exactly the gap Q15 of the Detailed form was written to close.

---

## 5. Stopped in the last 12 months

| Unit | Product | Vendor still holds data? |
|---|---|---|
| Athletics Performance | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Basketball (W) | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Communications | StatCrew | Not asked |
| Softball | YakkerTech | Not asked |

Four confirmed retirements, **zero known data dispositions**. Every one is an open
exposure with no owner.

---

## 6. Coming online

- **Athletics Performance** — Firstbeat, purchased, not yet in use.
- **Softball** — Trackman, about to be installed.

Neither appears to have gone through a documented vetting step. The Quick form did
not ask about the ITS IDEA form, so this cannot be confirmed here.

---

The Quick form has 5 questions. These questions from the Detailed (17-question) form
were never asked, so the spec's planned flags cannot be produced:

- Does it involve student-athlete information, and what kind? (Q6/Q7)
- How is it paid for, and when does the contract end? (Q9/Q10)
- **Did it go through the ITS IDEA form?** (Q11) — the bypass-rate number
- Does the vendor still hold data from discontinued products? (Q15)

inference, not a respondent answer.** Treat it as a screening list, not a finding.

    """Split on separators that sit outside parentheses and brackets.

    A naive text.split(",") breaks 'Routing (Magnum), replay (Dreamcatcher)'

    whenever a line contained a bracket. This does it properly.

    With split_sentences, a period followed by whitespace also ends a segment.
    A period with no space after it does not, so 'Athletic.net' survives.

# Athletics Technology Inventory — Findings

**Date:** 2026-08-29
**Source:** `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_2026-08-29.xlsx` — post-deadline export,
37 submissions (the earlier 2026-08-24 export had 15 and is kept in `raw/` for
comparison)
**Pipeline:** `scripts/clean_inventory.py` + `scripts/aliases.py` → `clean/*.csv`

---

## 1. Coverage

**37 submissions. 36 listed technology** — one was prose from a new hire who has
not received a laptop yet. **27 units responded** out of 34 on the list.

**7 did not respond:**

Golf (M) · Tennis (M) · Tennis (W) · Volleyball · Business Office · Marketing · Other

Two of those seven are probably not real gaps:

- **Marketing** — "Marketing and Fan Experience" responded. Almost certainly the
  same unit renamed on the live form.
- **Other** — never used by anyone. It looks like it was dropped once real units
  were added.

**So the genuine gaps are five: Golf (M), Tennis (M), Tennis (W), Volleyball, and
the Business Office.** That is roughly **85% coverage**, and the Business Office is
the one that matters most — it holds the contract records the framework wanted to
cross-check against.

Eight units submitted more than once: Football (3), Athletic Medicine (3), Baseball,
Basketball (M), Basketball (W), Track & Field / Cross Country, Athletic Mental Health
Services, Communications (2 each). These are different people describing different
slices of the same unit, so they were kept and tagged, not merged.

> **The unit list is not the one in the spec.** The Google Form spec lists 26
> options. The live Microsoft Form clearly differs — it produced answers like
> "Brand Engagement", "Spirit (Cheer, Dance, Mascots)", "Student Athlete Formation",
> "External/Revenue/Ticketing", "Equipment", "Broadcast and Big Screens" and
> "Development", none of which are on the spec's list. It also spells two units
> differently ("Track and Field/Cross Country", "Acrobatics and Tumbling"). Those
> spellings are now normalised, so both units correctly count as having responded.
> The working list is 34 units. Confirm it against the live form.

---

## 2. What is in the building

- **310 technology mentions**, resolving to **147 distinct products.**
  (14 further fragments were respondent section headers, sentence pieces, or
  physical equipment like helmets and jerseys. Those are tagged `excluded`, not
  counted.)
- **59 of 147 (40%) plausibly touch student-athlete information** — performance,
  medical, athlete-management, video-analytics, recruiting, or academic.
- **110 of 147 (75%) were named by exactly one unit.** Only 37 products are shared.

By category:

| Category | Distinct products |
|---|---|
| video-analytics | 19 |
| comms-media | 16 |
| performance | 15 |
| admin | 14 |
| broadcast | 13 |
| productivity | 12 |
| medical | 10 |
| office-general | 6 |
| recruiting | 6 |
| hardware | 5 |
| equipment-ops | 5 |
| academic | 5 |
| athlete-management | 4 |
| ai-general | 4 |
| facility | 4 |
| ticketing | 3 |
| food-travel | 2 |
| social-media | 1 |
| unidentified | 3 |

---

## 3. The long tail is the story

Three quarters of the software in this department is used by exactly one unit.
That is the population no central process is watching, and it is where surprises
live. Concretely, it includes AI tools nobody approved centrally (Claude, ChatGPT,
Gemini, Microsoft Copilot), a scatter of productivity apps (Notion, Asana, Todoist,
Padlet, Sling, GroupMe, WhatsApp, TeamUp), and one-off athlete-facing systems
(Nix Biosensors, Calera CORE, Boost Treadmills, C3 Logix, XO Armor, Hologic DXA).

Only a handful of platforms are genuinely departmental:

| Product | Units | Category |
|---|---|---|
| Teamworks | 12 | athlete-management |
| Microsoft Office | 11 | office-general |
| Adobe Creative Suite | 7 | office-general |
| Catapult | 6 | performance |
| Kitman Labs | 6 | athlete-management |
| VALD | 6 | performance |
| Box | 5 | admin |
| Canva | 5 | comms-media |
| Microsoft Teams | 4 | productivity |
| Greenfly | 3 | comms-media |
| Kinexon | 3 | performance |
| Perch | 3 | performance |
| Trackman | 3 | performance |

**Teamworks at 12 units is the only thing close to a department-wide system.**

---

## 4. Overlapping athlete-monitoring vendors

Athlete tracking runs on **Catapult (6 units), Kinexon (3), Polar (1)** with
**Firstbeat** arriving. Force and speed testing runs on **VALD (6), Perch (3),
GymAware, TMG**. Athlete management runs on **Teamworks (12), Kitman Labs (6)**
and **XPS Network**, which overlap heavily in function.

This is the consolidation conversation, and it is now answerable with real numbers
rather than estimates.

---

## 5. Polar is retired by two units and still running in a third

- **Athletics Performance** stopped using Polar Team Pro.
- **Basketball (W)** stopped using Polar Team Pro.
- **Basketball (M)** lists Polar as currently in use.

Nothing in the current process notices this. Whether the retiring units' athlete
data was deleted, exported, or is still sitting with the vendor is **not answerable
from this form.**

---

## 6. Stopped in the last 12 months

| Unit | Product | Vendor still holds data? |
|---|---|---|
| Athletics Performance | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Basketball (W) | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Athletic Medicine | Polaris GPS | Not asked |
| Communications | StatCrew | Not asked |
| Softball | YakkerTech | Not asked |
| Soccer | Hudl Focus | Not asked |
| Performance Nutrition | TikTok and X accounts | Not asked |

**Seven retirements, zero known data dispositions.** Every one is an open exposure
with no owner. This is the single most actionable gap in the dataset.

---

## 7. Coming online

- **Softball** — Trackman, about to be installed.
- **Athletics Performance** — Firstbeat, purchased, not yet in use.

Neither can be confirmed as having gone through a documented vetting step, because
the Quick form did not ask.

---

## 8. One respondent answered the real question unprompted

Broadcast and Big Screens opened their answer with:

> "Everything we have has gone through ITS approval, so they have the list already."

Then listed roughly 13 vendors — Ross Video, Evertz, Grass Valley, Calrec, Adder,
EditShare, Riedel, Daktronics, ANC, Haivision, Vyvx, LTN, Switch. Worth checking
against the ITS IDEA form history: if their list matches, that is a working
baseline for what compliance looks like. If it does not, the "ITS has the list
already" assumption is itself a finding.

---

## What this data still cannot answer

The Quick form has 5 questions. These were never asked, so the framework's planned
flags cannot be produced:

- Does it involve student-athlete information, and what kind?
- How is it paid for, and when does the contract end?
- **Did it go through the ITS IDEA form?** — the bypass-rate number
- Does the vendor still hold data from discontinued products?

The `athlete_data_likely` column is **my category inference, not a respondent
answer.** Treat it as a screening list, not a finding.

---

## Recommended next steps

1. **Chase five units:** Golf (M), Tennis (M), Tennis (W), Volleyball, and the
   Business Office. Confirm whether Marketing and "Marketing and Fan Experience"
   are the same unit while you are at it.
2. **Close the Polar loop.** Two units retired it, a third still runs it, and no
   one knows what the vendor kept. Small, concrete, demonstrable.
3. **Run the Detailed 17-question form as a second pass**, aimed at the 59
   athlete-data candidates in `clean/tech_master.csv`. This analysis produces that
   target list.
4. **Ask ITS for the IDEA form history** and diff it against
   `clean/tech_master.csv`. That gives the bypass number the framework needs, from
   two independent sources rather than a survey question.
5. **Decide on the long tail.** 110 single-unit products is a policy question, not
   a data question.

---

## Judgement calls worth a human eye

See the `review_note` column in `clean/tech_master.csv`:

- **Hudl** — merged "HUDL Statsbomb", "HUDL WyScout" and "HUDL Focus". Same vendor,
  three products. This is why Soccer shows as both using and having stopped Hudl.
- **Whistle** — one unit wrote "Whistle (DataViz)", others wrote bare "DataViz" and
  "GPS DataViz". Assumed to be the same thing.
- **Teamworks** — "TW Nutrition" and "Teamworks Hub" folded in as modules.
- **6-4-3 Charts** — merged Baseball's "643 Charts" and Softball's "6-4-3".
- **Social Media Platforms** — Instagram, TikTok, X and "social media apps
  primarily" bucketed together.
- **Evertz** — the broadcast answer was one run-on list. Only "Routing (Magnum)"
  and "replay (Dreamcatcher)" are read as Evertz; the rest are mapped to their own
  vendors.

**Three products could not be identified at all** and are sitting in
`clean/unmapped_review.csv`: **SCRL app** and **JABA** (Brand Engagement),
**Red Card** (Performance Nutrition). Ask those two units what they are.

Every other name mapping is explicit in `scripts/aliases.py`. Nothing was guessed
silently.

(Nix Biosensors, Calera CORE, Boost Treadmills, C3 Logix, XO Armor, Hologic DXA).

Only a handful of platforms are genuinely departmental:

| Product | Units | Category |

| Teamworks | 12 | athlete-management |
| Microsoft Office | 11 | office-general |
| Adobe Creative Suite | 7 | office-general |
| Catapult | 6 | performance |
| Kitman Labs | 6 | athlete-management |
| VALD | 6 | performance |
| Box | 5 | admin |
| Canva | 5 | comms-media |
| Microsoft Teams | 4 | productivity |
| Greenfly | 3 | comms-media |
| Kinexon | 3 | performance |
| Perch | 3 | performance |
| Trackman | 3 | performance |

**Teamworks at 12 units is the only thing close to a department-wide system.**

---

## 4. Overlapping athlete-monitoring vendors

Athlete tracking runs on **Catapult (6 units), Kinexon (3), Polar (1)** with
**Firstbeat** arriving. Force and speed testing runs on **VALD (6), Perch (3),
GymAware, TMG**. Athlete management runs on **Teamworks (12), Kitman Labs (6)**
and **XPS Network**, which overlap heavily in function.

This is the consolidation conversation, and it is now answerable with real numbers
rather than estimates.

---

## 5. Polar is retired by two units and still running in a third

- **Athletics Performance** stopped using Polar Team Pro.
- **Basketball (W)** stopped using Polar Team Pro.
- **Basketball (M)** lists Polar as currently in use.

Nothing in the current process notices this. Whether the retiring units' athlete
data was deleted, exported, or is still sitting with the vendor is **not answerable
from this form.**

---

## 6. Stopped in the last 12 months

| Unit | Product | Vendor still holds data? |
|---|---|---|
| Athletics Performance | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Basketball (W) | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Athletic Medicine | Polaris GPS | Not asked |
| Communications | StatCrew | Not asked |
| Softball | YakkerTech | Not asked |
| Soccer | Hudl Focus | Not asked |
| Performance Nutrition | TikTok and X accounts | Not asked |

**Seven retirements, zero known data dispositions.** Every one is an open exposure
with no owner. This is the single most actionable gap in the dataset.

---

## 7. Coming online

- **Softball** — Trackman, about to be installed.
- **Athletics Performance** — Firstbeat, purchased, not yet in use.

Neither can be confirmed as having gone through a documented vetting step, because
the Quick form did not ask.

---

## 8. One respondent answered the real question unprompted

Broadcast and Big Screens opened their answer with:

> "Everything we have has gone through ITS approval, so they have the list already."

Then listed roughly 13 vendors — Ross Video, Evertz, Grass Valley, Calrec, Adder,
EditShare, Riedel, Daktronics, ANC, Haivision, Vyvx, LTN, Switch. Worth checking
against the ITS IDEA form history: if their list matches, that is a working
baseline for what compliance looks like. If it does not, the "ITS has the list
already" assumption is itself a finding.

---

## What this data still cannot answer

The Quick form has 5 questions. These were never asked, so the framework's planned
flags cannot be produced:

- Does it involve student-athlete information, and what kind?
- How is it paid for, and when does the contract end?
- **Did it go through the ITS IDEA form?** — the bypass-rate number
- Does the vendor still hold data from discontinued products?

The `athlete_data_likely` column is **my category inference, not a respondent
answer.** Treat it as a screening list, not a finding.

---

## Recommended next steps

1. **Chase five units:** Golf (M), Tennis (M), Tennis (W), Volleyball, and the
   Business Office. Confirm whether Marketing and "Marketing and Fan Experience"
   are the same unit while you are at it.
2. **Close the Polar loop.** Two units retired it, a third still runs it, and no
   one knows what the vendor kept. Small, concrete, demonstrable.
3. **Run the Detailed 17-question form as a second pass**, aimed at the 59
   athlete-data candidates in `clean/tech_master.csv`. This analysis produces that
   target list.
4. **Ask ITS for the IDEA form history** and diff it against
   `clean/tech_master.csv`. That gives the bypass number the framework needs, from
   two independent sources rather than a survey question.
5. **Decide on the long tail.** 110 single-unit products is a policy question, not
   a data question.

---

See the `review_note` column in `clean/tech_master.csv`:

- **Hudl** — merged "HUDL Statsbomb", "HUDL WyScout" and "HUDL Focus". Same vendor,
  three products. This is why Soccer shows as both using and having stopped Hudl.
- **Whistle** — one unit wrote "Whistle (DataViz)", others wrote bare "DataViz" and
  "GPS DataViz". Assumed to be the same thing.
- **Teamworks** — "TW Nutrition" and "Teamworks Hub" folded in as modules.
- **6-4-3 Charts** — merged Baseball's "643 Charts" and Softball's "6-4-3".
- **Social Media Platforms** — Instagram, TikTok, X and "social media apps
  primarily" bucketed together.
- **Evertz** — the broadcast answer was one run-on list. Only "Routing (Magnum)"
  and "replay (Dreamcatcher)" are read as Evertz; the rest are mapped to their own
  vendors.

**Three products could not be identified at all** and are sitting in
`clean/unmapped_review.csv`: **SCRL app** and **JABA** (Brand Engagement),
**Red Card** (Performance Nutrition). Ask those two units what they are.

Every other name mapping is explicit in `scripts/aliases.py`. Nothing was guessed
silently.

# Tech_Inventory_Analysis

Cleaning and analysis of the Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory survey.

Companion to `~/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework`, which holds the framework
documents, the form specs, and the form links. This folder holds only the
collected data and what comes out of it.

## Layout

```
raw/     frozen survey exports, date-stamped. never edited.
scripts/ clean_inventory.py (parser) + aliases.py (all judgement calls)
clean/   generated CSVs. delete and regenerate freely.
docs/    findings
deliverables/  anything that goes to Kenny / Jon Allen / ITS
```

## Run

```bash
cd ~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis
uv run --with openpyxl python3 scripts/clean_inventory.py
```
