# Athletics Technology Inventory — Findings

**Date:** 2026-08-29
**Status:** Interim. Applied Performance's own deadline was 29 August; the
department-wide soft deadline set at the 24 August all-staff meeting is
**29 September**, so collection is still open.
**Source:** `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_2026-08-29.xlsx` — export taken 29 August,
37 submissions (the earlier 2026-08-24 export had 15 and is kept in `raw/` for
comparison)
**Pipeline:** `scripts/clean_inventory.py` + `scripts/aliases.py` → `clean/*.csv`

---

## 1. Coverage

**37 submissions. 36 listed technology** — one was prose from a new hire who has
not received a laptop yet. **27 units responded** out of 33 on the list.

**6 had not responded as of 29 August:**

Golf (M) · Tennis (M) · Tennis (W) · Volleyball · Business Office · Other

One of those six is not a real gap: **"Other"** was never used by anyone and looks
like it was dropped from the live form once real units were added.

("Marketing and Fan Experience" is confirmed by Eric as what the Marketing
department is now called. The two are merged, so Marketing counts as having
responded.)

**So five units are still outstanding: Golf (M), Tennis (M), Tennis (W),
Volleyball, and the Business Office.** That is roughly **85% coverage with a month
still to run.** The Business Office is the one worth a direct ask — it holds the
contract records this inventory is designed to be read against.

Eight units submitted more than once: Football (3), Athletic Medicine (3), Baseball,
Basketball (M), Basketball (W), Track & Field / Cross Country, Athletic Mental Health
Services, Communications (2 each). These are different people describing different
slices of the same unit, so they were kept and tagged, not merged.

> **The unit list is not the one in the spec.** The Google Form spec lists 26
> options. The live Microsoft Form clearly differs — it produced answers like
> "Brand Engagement", "Spirit (Cheer, Dance, Mascots)", "Student Athlete Formation",
> "External/Revenue/Ticketing", "Equipment", "Broadcast and Big Screens" and
> "Development", none of which are on the spec's list. It also spells two units
> differently ("Track and Field/Cross Country", "Acrobatics and Tumbling"). Those
> spellings are now normalised, so both units correctly count as having responded.
> The working list is 33 units. Confirm it against the live form.

---

## 2. What is in the building

- **310 technology mentions**, resolving to **147 distinct products.**
  (14 further fragments were respondent section headers, sentence pieces, or
  physical equipment like helmets and jerseys. Those are tagged `excluded`, not
  counted.)
- **60 of 147 (41%) plausibly touch student-athlete information** — performance,
  medical, athlete-management, video-analytics, recruiting, academic, or the
  athlete meal-money stipend.
- **110 of 147 (75%) were named by exactly one unit.** Only 37 products are shared.

By category:

| Category | Distinct products |
|---|---|
| video-analytics | 19 |
| comms-media | 16 |
| performance | 15 |
| admin | 14 |
| broadcast | 13 |
| productivity | 12 |
| medical | 10 |
| office-general | 6 |
| recruiting | 6 |
| hardware | 5 |
| equipment-ops | 5 |
| academic | 5 |
| athlete-management | 4 |
| ai-general | 4 |
| facility | 4 |
| ticketing | 3 |
| food-travel | 2 |
| athlete-stipend | 1 |
| social-media | 1 |
| unidentified | 2 |

---

## 3. The long tail is the story

Three quarters of the software in this department is used by exactly one unit.
That is the population no central process is watching, and it is where surprises
live. Concretely, it includes AI tools nobody approved centrally (Claude, ChatGPT,
Gemini, Microsoft Copilot), a scatter of productivity apps (Notion, Asana, Todoist,
Padlet, Sling, GroupMe, WhatsApp, TeamUp), and one-off athlete-facing systems
(Nix Biosensors, Calera CORE, Boost Treadmills, C3 Logix, XO Armor, Hologic DXA).

Only a handful of platforms are genuinely departmental:

| Product | Units | Category |
|---|---|---|
| Teamworks | 12 | athlete-management |
| Microsoft Office | 11 | office-general |
| Adobe Creative Suite | 7 | office-general |
| Catapult | 6 | performance |
| Kitman Labs | 6 | athlete-management |
| VALD | 6 | performance |
| Box | 5 | admin |
| Canva | 5 | comms-media |
| Microsoft Teams | 4 | productivity |
| Greenfly | 3 | comms-media |
| Kinexon | 3 | performance |
| Perch | 3 | performance |
| Trackman | 3 | performance |

**Teamworks at 12 units is the only thing close to a department-wide system.**

---

## 4. Overlapping athlete-monitoring vendors

Athlete tracking runs on **Catapult (6 units), Kinexon (3), Polar (1)** with
**Firstbeat** arriving. Force and speed testing runs on **VALD (6), Perch (3),
GymAware, TMG**. Athlete management runs on **Teamworks (12), Kitman Labs (6)**
and **XPS Network**, which overlap heavily in function.

This is the consolidation conversation, and it is now answerable with real numbers
rather than estimates.

---

## 5. Polar is retired by two units and still running in a third

- **Athletics Performance** stopped using Polar Team Pro.
- **Basketball (W)** stopped using Polar Team Pro.
- **Basketball (M)** lists Polar as currently in use.

Surfacing that automatically, and confirming what a vendor retains when a unit
stops using a product, are two capabilities the framework would add. Whether the
retiring units' athlete data was deleted, exported, or is still held by the vendor
is **not answerable from this form.**

---

## 6. Stopped in the last 12 months

| Unit | Product | Vendor still holds data? |
|---|---|---|
| Athletics Performance | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Basketball (W) | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Athletic Medicine | Polaris GPS | Not asked |
| Communications | StatCrew | Not asked |
| Softball | YakkerTech | Not asked |
| Soccer | Hudl Focus | Not asked |
| Performance Nutrition | TikTok and X accounts | Not asked |

**Seven retirements, no recorded data disposition.** The short form did not ask,
so the answer simply is not captured anywhere yet. Confirming what each vendor
retained is the most concrete, closeable action in this dataset.

---

## 7. Coming online

- **Softball** — Trackman, about to be installed.
- **Athletics Performance** — Firstbeat, purchased, not yet in use.

Neither can be confirmed as having gone through a documented vetting step, because
the Quick form did not ask.

---

## 8. One respondent answered the real question unprompted

Broadcast and Big Screens opened their answer with:

> "Everything we have has gone through ITS approval, so they have the list already."

Then listed roughly 13 vendors — Ross Video, Evertz, Grass Valley, Calrec, Adder,
EditShare, Riedel, Daktronics, ANC, Haivision, Vyvx, LTN, Switch. Worth checking
against the ITS IDEA form history: if their list matches, that is a working
baseline for what compliance looks like. If it does not, the "ITS has the list
already" assumption is itself a finding.

---

## What this data still cannot answer

The Quick form has 5 questions. These were never asked, so the framework's planned
flags cannot be produced:

- Does it involve student-athlete information, and what kind?
- How is it paid for, and when does the contract end?
- **Did it go through the ITS IDEA form?** — the bypass-rate number
- Does the vendor still hold data from discontinued products?

The `athlete_data_likely` column is **my category inference, not a respondent
answer.** Treat it as a screening list, not a finding.

---

## Recommended next steps

1. **Follow up with five units before 29 September:** Golf (M), Tennis (M),
   Tennis (W), Volleyball, and the Business Office.
2. **Close the Polar loop.** Two units retired it, a third still runs it, and no
   one knows what the vendor kept. Small, concrete, demonstrable.
3. **Run the Detailed 17-question form as a second pass**, aimed at the 60
   athlete-data candidates in `clean/tech_master.csv`. This analysis produces that
   target list.
4. **Ask ITS for the IDEA form history** and diff it against
   `clean/tech_master.csv`. That gives the bypass number the framework needs, from
   two independent sources rather than a survey question.
5. **Decide on the long tail.** 110 single-unit products is a policy question, not
   a data question.

---

## Judgement calls worth a human eye

See the `review_note` column in `clean/tech_master.csv`:

- **Hudl** — merged "HUDL Statsbomb", "HUDL WyScout" and "HUDL Focus". Same vendor,
  three products. This is why Soccer shows as both using and having stopped Hudl.
- **Whistle** — one unit wrote "Whistle (DataViz)", others wrote bare "DataViz" and
  "GPS DataViz". Assumed to be the same thing.
- **Teamworks** — "TW Nutrition" and "Teamworks Hub" folded in as modules.
- **6-4-3 Charts** — merged Baseball's "643 Charts" and Softball's "6-4-3".
- **Social Media Platforms** — Instagram, TikTok, X and "social media apps
  primarily" bucketed together.
- **Evertz** — the broadcast answer was one run-on list. Only "Routing (Magnum)"
  and "replay (Dreamcatcher)" are read as Evertz; the rest are mapped to their own
  vendors.

- **Red Card** — identified by Eric as the student-athlete meal-money stipend,
  redeemable at selected local vendors. It carries athlete identity and
  transaction records, so it is categorised as athlete data and belongs in the
  detailed second pass even though it is not a performance system.

**Two products could not be identified at all** and are sitting in
`clean/unmapped_review.csv`: **SCRL app** and **JABA**, both named by Brand
Engagement. Eric is checking what they are.

Every other name mapping is explicit in `scripts/aliases.py`. Nothing was guessed
silently.

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/html-to-pdf

# HTML to PDF

Headless-Chrome render of a local HTML file to PDF. No manual browser printing.

## Quick start

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File "$HOME\.claude\skills\html-to-pdf\scripts\html2pdf.ps1" -HtmlPath "report.html"
# optional explicit output:
#   ... -HtmlPath "report.html" -OutPdf "C:\path\coach-report.pdf"
```

Defaults: same folder, same name, `.pdf` extension. Report the output path and size to the user when done.

## Page setup lives in the HTML, not in flags

Headless Chrome takes page size/orientation from CSS `@page`. If the source lacks one, inject a style block before rendering (edit the file or a temp copy):

```html
<style>
  @page { size: Letter portrait; margin: 12mm; }        /* or: Letter landscape */
  body { -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact; }
</style>
```

- `print-color-adjust: exact` keeps background colors/graphics — the equivalent of ticking "Background graphics" in the print dialog. Coach-facing reports almost always need it.
- Landscape decks: `size: Letter landscape`. Slide decks sized in `vh/vw` may need a fixed pixel size instead, e.g. `@page { size: 1280px 720px; margin: 0; }`.

## Edge cases

- **Animated/reveal-on-scroll pages** (frontend-slides output): elements hidden until an IntersectionObserver fires will print blank. Add a print override: `@media print { .slide, [data-reveal] { opacity: 1 !important; transform: none !important; } }`.
- **Multi-slide decks**: force one slide per page with `.slide { page-break-after: always; height: auto; }` inside `@media print`.
- **External images that fail to load**: headless Chrome won't wait forever; if images are missing in the PDF, ensure they're local paths or add `--virtual-time-budget=5000` to the Chrome args in the script call.
- **Fonts**: Google Fonts load fine (network is available); if a font is missing, the PDF silently falls back — spot-check the output.

## Verify

Always open/inspect the produced PDF (Read the file or check page count/size) before telling the user it's done — a 2 KB PDF is a blank render.

skills.name: dataviz
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.251/82f6633fd1f115a129d847bcd7b44fa6/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

skills.name: artifact-design
skills.content:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page - what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in. Format is not part of this read: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it - a Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title and takes almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first - CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world - its materials, instruments, vernacular - is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. Google Fonts is the one font host the Artifact CSP admits - link it directly (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&display=swap">`); a face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI or it falls back silently. Either way, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Load libraries, don't paste them.** When the page genuinely needs a library - React, a charting or highlighting package - load its UMD build from cdnjs (only the script - a library's stylesheet still has to be inlined) with one pinned `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` placed before the inline script that uses its global, instead of inlining the library's source or hand-writing a stand-in; the Artifact tool's description lists the few other script hosts the CSP admits. The page's own CSS and JS, its images and its data ship with the page. Most pages need no library at all - reach for one only when it carries real weight.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject - the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states, not two: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps *nothing* - most viewers see the un-stamped document, where only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Structure the CSS token-level for all three: the bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice beats a dark OS; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also wins in the other direction. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block - a color whose only definition sits behind `[data-theme]` never applies in the un-stamped state, and the page renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground. Two more rules keep each theme resolving as a set: the artifact composites over a ground the viewer paints in *its* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token - a transparent body silently borrows the host's ground; and every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never a literal that only works in one theme. Before publishing, scan the stylesheet for any color declared only inside a media or `[data-theme]` block - that is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first - don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme - then skip the media query and stamps entirely but still paint the background and every color explicitly, so the page holds on either host ground; make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content - tables, code, diagrams - gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly - their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out - a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen - name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it - no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Name the page like a product, not a caption.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it sets the reader's first impression of care. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject - or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which is then the page's name. Stop at the name - a title that carries its own explainer after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it sits beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could sit on any of them fails as a name just as surely as an appended explainer. When a candidate title pairs the name with a generic word - a greeting, a category, a page-type label - the name is the half to keep; a trim that drops the identity and keeps the generic word produces exactly the title that could sit on any page. And the rule removes explainers, it does not impose brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. The one-sentence publish `description` is where the explanation belongs; the gallery shows it right under the title.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number - a pill, a chip, a severity stripe - so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan - a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4-6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles - a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world - headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

skills.name: project
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/project

# /project — portfolio registry skill

Drives the shipped `project-triage` CLI to capture ideas, log progress, and
keep the front-burner dashboard current. The registry (`portfolio.json`) is
the single source of truth — never hand-edit `dashboard.html`.

## Paths

- Repo: `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage`
- Interpreter: `python3`
- Registry: `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.json`
- CLI entry points: `portfolio.py` (mutations), `render.py` (render)
- Generated: `dashboard.html`, `pulse.md` (both written next to the scripts;
  do not edit by hand, they are regenerated every render)

## CLI contract (verbatim — do not alter flags)

```
& "python3" "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py" add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<source>"
& "python3" "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py" add-update "<name>" "<note>" --next-action "<optional>"
& "python3" "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py" set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"
& "python3" "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/render.py"
& "python3" "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/render.py" --no-scan
```

- `add-idea` prints `idea captured (<N> in inbox)`.
- `add-update` prints `updated <name>` (name match is case-insensitive).
- `set-stage` prints `stage set: <name> → <stage>`. Valid stages, in ladder
  order: `idea grilled spec planned building shipped`.
- `render.py` (full scan) prints `wrote dashboard.html · wrote pulse.md · ...`.
- `render.py --no-scan` does the same but skips the DEV/ activity heuristics
  (fast; use it after any registry mutation, and to validate hand-edits).
- Any error path prints `[error] <msg>` to stderr and exits 2, with no
  mutation to `portfolio.json`. Stop and surface the message verbatim.

## Verbs

### `idea <pitch>`
Run `add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<conversation context, ≤8 words>"`. The
source should summarize where the idea came from (e.g. "chat about GPS
vendor gaps"), not just "chat". Then do the render + republish ritual.

### `update <name> <note>`
Fuzzy-match `<name>` against the project names currently in the registry
(read `portfolio.json` first). If exactly one match, run `add-update "<name>"
"<note>"` (add `--next-action "<...>"` if the user gave one). If the match is
ambiguous or there's no close match, ask the user which project they mean
before running anything. Then do the render + republish ritual.

### `rank`
Read `portfolio.json`, show both lanes' active projects with their current
`rank` values, and ask for the new order. Never reorder ranks yourself —
only apply the order the user gives you. Rewrite the `rank` fields directly
with the Edit tool, then validate by running `render.py --no-scan` (exit 0
means the edit is structurally valid). Then do the render + republish
ritual (this counts as the render step — no need to run render.py twice).

### `promote <idea>`
Ask which lane (`job` or `side`) and for a `next_action`. With the Edit
tool: set the matching idea's `status` to `promoted`, and append a new
project entry to that lane at the next free `rank` (max existing rank in
that lane + 1). Validate with `render.py --no-scan`, then do the render +
republish ritual.

### `stage <name> <stage>`
Fuzzy-match `<name>` like `update` does. Run `set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"`.
The dashboard auto-detects spec/plan docs (in the project's DEV folder under
`docs/specs`, `docs/plans`, or the `docs/superpowers/...` variants) and
renders plan-checkbox progress — the stage is your curated claim; drift
between the two shows on the card. Then do the render + republish ritual.

**Shipped → harvest handoff:** when the stage being set is `shipped`, after
the ritual offer once: "Want me to run /harvest on <name> to distill it into

## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the Word version of the technology inventory findings.

Run:
    uv run --with python-docx python3 scripts/build_docx.py

Reads the generated CSVs in clean/ so the document can never drift from the
data. Prose is held here rather than parsed out of the HTML, because the two
formats want different phrasing.

House rules applied, from Kenny Boyd's review history on the framework docs:
  - Baylor branding in the header, document status on every page.
  - No language implying the department was previously incompetent. Findings
    are written as capability the framework would add, not as failure.
  - Neutral, descriptive labels. Nothing that ranks a unit.
"""

import csv
import os
import sys

from docx import Document
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
CLEAN = os.path.join(ROOT, "clean")
OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "deliverables",
                   "Tech_Inventory_FINDINGS_ER_2026-08-29.docx")

GREEN = RGBColor(0x15, 0x47, 0x34)     # Baylor green
GOLD = RGBColor(0x8A, 0x64, 0x10)
INK = RGBColor(0x10, 0x1E, 0x18)
MUTED = RGBColor(0x5C, 0x6B, 0x63)

BODY_FONT = "Calibri"
HEAD_FONT = "Cambria"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# data
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load():
    def rd(name):
        with open(os.path.join(CLEAN, name), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return list(csv.DictReader(f))

    master = [r for r in rd("tech_master.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    long = [r for r in rd("tech_inventory_long.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    cov = rd("coverage.csv")
    stopped = rd("stopped_using.csv")
    unmapped = rd("unmapped_review.csv")
    return master, long, cov, stopped, unmapped


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def style_base(doc):
    st = doc.styles["Normal"]
    st.font.name = BODY_FONT
    st.font.size = Pt(10.5)
    st.font.color.rgb = INK
    st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(7)
    st.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.14


def para(doc, text, size=10.5, bold=False, italic=False, color=INK,
         space_before=0, space_after=7, font=BODY_FONT, align=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment = align
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(space_before)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    add_runs(p, text, size=size, bold=bold, italic=italic, color=color, font=font)
    return p


def add_runs(p, text, size=10.5, bold=False, italic=False, color=INK,
             font=BODY_FONT):
    """Split on ** ** so bold can be inlined in the source strings."""
    for i, chunk in enumerate(text.split("**")):
        if not chunk:
            continue
        r = p.add_run(chunk)
        r.font.name = font
        r.font.size = Pt(size)
        r.font.color.rgb = color
        r.bold = bold or (i % 2 == 1)
        r.italic = italic
    return p


def h1(doc, text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
    r = p.add_run(text)
    r.font.name = HEAD_FONT
    r.font.size = Pt(22)
    r.font.color.rgb = GREEN
    r.bold = True
    return p


def h2(doc, tag, text):
    """Section heading with a small uppercase tag above it."""
    t = doc.add_paragraph()
    t.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(16)
    t.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
    r = t.add_run(tag.upper())
    r.font.name = BODY_FONT
    r.font.size = Pt(7.5)
    r.font.color.rgb = GOLD
    r.bold = True

        if i in numeric_cols:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the one-page executive summary of the technology inventory.

Run:
    uv run --with python-docx python3 scripts/build_exec_summary.py

This is the leadership-facing document. It exists because Kenny Boyd asked, in
the 13 August technology review, for "the more simple and concise, almost like
one page checklist". The ten-page findings report stays as the analyst's
working document; this is the one that gets forwarded.

Every figure is read from clean/*.csv, so the summary cannot drift from the
findings report or from the data.

Format follows the established pattern in
05_SYSTEMS/SoftwareTechDocs/Software_and_Tech_Management_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_*.docx:
Baylor wordmark, title, "Executive Summary", a status block, then short
sections. House rules from Kenny's review history apply - no wording that
implies the department was previously failing, no labels that rank a unit,
document status visible on the page.

One page is a hard constraint, not a goal. verify_pages() renders the file
through Word and fails the build if it spills to two.
"""

import csv
import os
import subprocess
import sys

from docx import Document
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from build_docx import (  # noqa: E402  - shared house style, single source
    GREEN, GOLD, INK, MUTED, BODY_FONT, HEAD_FONT,
    style_base, para, add_runs, h2, bottom_rule, table, page_field,
)

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
CLEAN = os.path.join(ROOT, "clean")
DELIV = os.path.join(ROOT, "deliverables")
STEM = "Tech_Inventory_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_2026-08-29"
OUT = os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".docx")

GREY = RGBColor(0x59, 0x59, 0x59)

# The "Other" option was never selected by anyone and looks like a leftover
# from the draft form, so it is not counted as a unit that owes a response.
PHANTOM_UNITS = {"Other"}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# data
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load():
    def rd(name):
        with open(os.path.join(CLEAN, name), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return list(csv.DictReader(f))

    master = [r for r in rd("tech_master.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    long = [r for r in rd("tech_inventory_long.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    return master, long, rd("coverage.csv"), rd("stopped_using.csv")


def figures():
    master, long, cov, stopped = load()

    cov = [r for r in cov if r["unit"] not in PHANTOM_UNITS]
    units_total = len(cov)
    units_in = len([r for r in cov if r["status"] in ("responded", "MULTIPLE")])
    outstanding = [r["unit"] for r in cov if r["status"] == "NO RESPONSE"]

    n_products = len(master)
    n_athlete = len([r for r in master if r["athlete_data_likely"] == "Y"])
    n_single = len([r for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) == 1])
    top = max(master, key=lambda r: int(r["unit_count"]))

    # One respondent wrote prose instead of a product list (a new hire still
    # waiting on a laptop), so submissions is one more than parsed responses.
    n_sub = len({r["response_id"] for r in long}) + 1

    return dict(
        units_total=units_total, units_in=units_in, outstanding=outstanding,
        n_sub=n_sub, n_mentions=len(long), n_products=n_products,
        n_athlete=n_athlete, pct_athlete=round(100 * n_athlete / n_products),
        n_single=n_single, pct_single=round(100 * n_single / n_products),
        top_name=top["canonical"], top_units=int(top["unit_count"]),
        n_stopped=len(stopped),
        pct_units=round(100 * units_in / units_total),
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# page furniture
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def page_setup(doc):
    """Tighter margins than the findings report - this has one page to work in."""
    sec = doc.sections[0]
    sec.top_margin = Inches(0.7)
    sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.6)
    sec.left_margin = Inches(0.75)
    sec.right_margin = Inches(0.75)

    hp = sec.header.paragraphs[0]
    hp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT
    r = hp.add_run("BAYLOR ATHLETICS  ·  APPLIED PERFORMANCE")
    r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(8); r.bold = True
    r.font.color.rgb = GREEN
    r2 = hp.add_run("        INTERIM — COLLECTION OPEN TO 29 SEPTEMBER 2026")
    r2.font.name = BODY_FONT; r2.font.size = Pt(8); r2.font.color.rgb = GOLD
    r2.bold = True
    bottom_rule(hp)

    fp = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
    fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT
    fr = fp.add_run("Athletics Technology Inventory  ·  Executive Summary  "
                    "·  29 August 2026  ·  E. Rash        ")
    fr.font.name = BODY_FONT; fr.font.size = Pt(8); fr.font.color.rgb = MUTED
    page_field(fp)


def title_block(doc):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
    r = p.add_run("BAYLOR ATHLETICS")
    r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(11); r.bold = True
    r.font.color.rgb = GREEN

    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
    r = p.add_run("Athletics Technology Inventory")
    r.font.name = HEAD_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(19); r.bold = True
    r.font.color.rgb = GREEN

    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(8)
    r = p.add_run("Executive Summary")
    r.font.name = HEAD_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(13); r.bold = True
    r.font.color.rgb = GREY


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# document
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build(f):
    doc = Document()
    style_base(doc)
    page_setup(doc)
    title_block(doc)

    table(doc,
          ["Status", "Interim — collection open to the department "
                     "soft deadline of 29 September 2026"],
          [["Date", "August 29, 2026"],
           ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics"],
           ["Companion documents",
            "Athletics Technology Inventory — Findings (full report); "
            "Software and Technology Management Framework"]],
          widths=[1.55, 5.45])

    # ---- in brief --------------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "In brief", "What we asked, and where it stands")
    para(doc,
         "Every unit was asked a five-question survey naming the technology it "
         "uses. **{units_in} of {units_total} units have answered so far**, "
         "describing **{n_products} distinct products**. Unit leaders have "
         "until 29 September to complete the remaining responses, so the "
         "figures below are an interim read rather than a final count."
         .format(**f),
         space_after=8)

    # ---- the numbers -----------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "Coverage", "The inventory in eight numbers")
    table(doc,
          ["Measure", "As of 29 August 2026"],
          [["Units that have responded",
            "**{units_in} of {units_total}**  ({pct_units}%)".format(**f)],
           ["Units still to respond",
            "**{}** — {}".format(len(f["outstanding"]),
                                 ", ".join(f["outstanding"]))],
           ["Submissions received", "**{n_sub}**".format(**f)],
           ["Distinct products named",
            "**{n_products}**, from {n_mentions} mentions".format(**f)],
           ["Products that likely involve student-athlete information",
            "**{n_athlete}**  ({pct_athlete}% of products)".format(**f)],
           ["Products named by one unit only",
            "**{n_single}**  ({pct_single}% of products)".format(**f)],
           ["Most widely shared system",
            "**{top_name}**, used by {top_units} units".format(**f)],
           ["Products retired in the last 12 months",
            "**{n_stopped}**".format(**f)]],
          widths=[3.05, 3.95])

    # ---- reading ---------------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "Reading", "Three things the numbers show")
    for text in [
        "**Most software sits with a single unit.** {n_single} of the "
        "{n_products} products were named by one unit only. A shared record of "
        "what is in use is the capability that makes this population visible."
        .format(**f),

        "**One system is close to department-wide.** {top_name}, at {top_units} "
        "units. There is no comparable second, so a single place to look does "
        "not exist yet — which is what this inventory begins to build."
        .format(**f),

        "**{n_stopped} products were retired in the last year.** What each "
        "vendor still holds was not asked on the short form, so it is not yet "
        "recorded anywhere. This is the smallest and most closeable gap in the "
        "dataset.".format(**f),
    ]:
        p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet")
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
        add_runs(p, text, size=10)

    # ---- the checklist ---------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "Next", "Checklist")
    table(doc,
          ["", "Action", "Owner", "By"],
          [["", "Collect the {} outstanding unit responses.".format(
              len(f["outstanding"])), "Unit leaders", "29 Sept 2026"],
           ["", "Confirm what each vendor retained for the {n_stopped} retired "
                "products.".format(**f), "Applied Performance", "Oct 2026"],
           ["", "Compare the inventory against the ITS IDEA form history.",
            "Applied Performance / ITS", "Oct 2026"],
           ["", "Run the detailed review form on the {n_athlete} products that "
                "involve athlete information.".format(**f),
            "Applied Performance", "Nov 2026"],
           ["", "Decide how single-unit products are handled going forward.",
            "Senior staff", "Nov 2026"]],
          widths=[0.28, 3.72, 1.75, 1.25])

    doc.save(OUT)
    return OUT


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# verification
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def to_pdf(docx_path):
    """Export through Word. No LibreOffice on this machine, and Word is the
    renderer the audience will open the file in anyway."""
    pdf_path = os.path.splitext(docx_path)[0] + ".pdf"
    if os.path.exists(pdf_path):
        os.remove(pdf_path)
    script = '''
    tell application "Microsoft Word"
        set wasRunning to running
        open POSIX file "{docx}"
        set d to active document
        save as d file name POSIX file "{pdf}" file format format PDF
        close d saving no
        if not wasRunning then quit
    end tell
    '''.format(docx=docx_path, pdf=pdf_path)
    subprocess.run(["osascript", "-e", script], check=True,
                   capture_output=True, text=True)
    return pdf_path


def page_count(pdf_path):
    import pypdfium2 as pdfium
    return len(pdfium.PdfDocument(pdf_path))


def main():
    f = figures()
    out = build(f)
    print("wrote", out)
    pdf = to_pdf(out)
    n = page_count(pdf)
    print("wrote", pdf, "->", n, "page(s)")
    if n != 1:
        sys.exit("[error] executive summary must be one page, rendered {}".format(n))
    print("one page confirmed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    fr = fp.add_run("Athletics Technology Inventory  ·  Executive Summary  "
                    "·  29 August 2026  ·  E. Rash        ")
    fr.font.name = BODY_FONT; fr.font.size = Pt(8); fr.font.color.rgb = MUTED
    page_field(fp)


def title_block(doc):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
    r = p.add_run("BAYLOR ATHLETICS")
    r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(11); r.bold = True
    r.font.color.rgb = GREEN

    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
    r = p.add_run("Athletics Technology Inventory")
    r.font.name = HEAD_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(19); r.bold = True
    r.font.color.rgb = GREEN

    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(8)
    r = p.add_run("Executive Summary")
    r.font.name = HEAD_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(13); r.bold = True
    r.font.color.rgb = GREY


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# document
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build(f):
    doc = Document()
    style_base(doc)
    page_setup(doc)
    title_block(doc)

    table(doc,
          ["Status", "Interim — collection open to the department "
                     "soft deadline of 29 September 2026"],
          [["Date", "August 29, 2026"],
           ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics"],
           ["Companion documents",
            "Athletics Technology Inventory — Findings (full report); "
            "Software and Technology Management Framework"]],
          widths=[1.55, 5.45])

    # ---- in brief --------------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "In brief", "What we asked, and where it stands")
    para(doc,
         "Every unit was asked a five-question survey naming the technology it "
         "uses. **{units_in} of {units_total} units have answered so far**, "
         "describing **{n_products} distinct products**. Unit leaders have "
         "until 29 September to complete the remaining responses, so the "
         "figures below are an interim read rather than a final count."
         .format(**f),
         space_after=8)

    # ---- the numbers -----------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "Coverage", "The inventory in eight numbers")
    table(doc,
          ["Measure", "As of 29 August 2026"],
          [["Units that have responded",
            "**{units_in} of {units_total}**  ({pct_units}%)".format(**f)],
           ["Units still to respond",
            "**{}** — {}".format(len(f["outstanding"]),
                                 ", ".join(f["outstanding"]))],
           ["Submissions received", "**{n_sub}**".format(**f)],
           ["Distinct products named",
            "**{n_products}**, from {n_mentions} mentions".format(**f)],
           ["Products that likely involve student-athlete information",
            "**{n_athlete}**  ({pct_athlete}% of products)".format(**f)],
           ["Products named by one unit only",
            "**{n_single}**  ({pct_single}% of products)".format(**f)],
           ["Most widely shared system",
            "**{top_name}**, used by {top_units} units".format(**f)],
           ["Products retired in the last 12 months",
            "**{n_stopped}**".format(**f)]],
          widths=[3.05, 3.95])

    # ---- reading ---------------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "Reading", "Three things the numbers show")
    for text in [
        "**Most software sits with a single unit.** {n_single} of the "
        "{n_products} products were named by one unit only. A shared record of "
        "what is in use is the capability that makes this population visible."
        .format(**f),

        "**One system is close to department-wide.** {top_name}, at {top_units} "
        "units. There is no comparable second, so a single place to look does "
        "not exist yet — which is what this inventory begins to build."
        .format(**f),

        "**{n_stopped} products were retired in the last year.** What each "
        "vendor still holds was not asked on the short form, so it is not yet "
        "recorded anywhere. This is the smallest and most closeable gap in the "
        "dataset.".format(**f),
    ]:
        p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet")
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
        add_runs(p, text, size=10)

    # ---- the checklist ---------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "Next", "Checklist")
    table(doc,
          ["", "Action", "Owner", "By"],
          [["", "Collect the {} outstanding unit responses.".format(
              len(f["outstanding"])), "Unit leaders", "29 Sept 2026"],
           ["", "Confirm what each vendor retained for the {n_stopped} retired "
                "products.".format(**f), "Applied Performance", "Oct 2026"],
           ["", "Compare the inventory against the ITS IDEA form history.",
            "Applied Performance / ITS", "Oct 2026"],
           ["", "Run the detailed review form on the {n_athlete} products that "
                "involve athlete information.".format(**f),
            "Applied Performance", "Nov 2026"],
           ["", "Decide how single-unit products are handled going forward.",
            "Senior staff", "Nov 2026"]],
          widths=[0.28, 3.72, 1.75, 1.25])

    doc.save(OUT)
    return OUT


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# verification
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def to_pdf(docx_path):
    """Export through Word. No LibreOffice on this machine, and Word is the
    renderer the audience will open the file in anyway."""
    pdf_path = os.path.splitext(docx_path)[0] + ".pdf"
    if os.path.exists(pdf_path):
        os.remove(pdf_path)
    script = '''
    tell application "Microsoft Word"
        set wasRunning to running
        open POSIX file "{docx}"
        set d to active document
        save as d file name POSIX file "{pdf}" file format format PDF
        close d saving no
        if not wasRunning then quit
    end tell
    '''.format(docx=docx_path, pdf=pdf_path)
    subprocess.run(["osascript", "-e", script], check=True,
                   capture_output=True, text=True)
    return pdf_path


def page_count(pdf_path):
    import pypdfium2 as pdfium
    return len(pdfium.PdfDocument(pdf_path))


def main():
    f = figures()
    out = build(f)
    print("wrote", out)
    pdf = to_pdf(out)
    n = page_count(pdf)
    print("wrote", pdf, "->", n, "page(s)")
    if n != 1:
        sys.exit("[error] executive summary must be one page, rendered {}".format(n))
    print("one page confirmed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Build the one-page executive summary of the technology inventory. Run: uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_exec_summary.py This is the leadership-facing document. It exists because Kenny Boyd asked, in the 13 August technology review, for "the more simple and concise, almost like one page checklist". The ten-page findings report stays as the analyst's working document; this is the one that gets forwarded. Two outputs, one source: content() -> the document, as data |-> render_docx() the editable Word file |-> render_html() a print twin, rendered to PDF by headless Chrome The prose and the figures are written once, in content(), so the .docx and the .pdf cannot say different things. Every number is read from clean/*.csv, so neither can drift from the findings report. Why Chrome and not Word: Word on this machine will not accept AppleScript automation from a non-interactive session - it opens the file and then blocks, apparently on a dialog that is not visible to the caller. The HTML twin uses the same page geometry, the same fonts (Calibri and Cambria, both installed with Office) and the same point sizes, so its page count is a faithful check on whether the content fits one page. House rules from Kenny's review history apply: no wording that implies the department was previously failing, no labels that rank a unit, document status visible on the page. """ import csv import os import subprocess import sys from docx import Document from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))) from build_docx import ( # noqa: E402 - shared house style, single source GREEN, GOLD, INK, MUTED, BODY_FONT, HEAD_FONT, style_base, para, add_runs, bottom_rule, table, page_field, shade, ) ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))) CLEAN = os.path.join(ROOT, "clean") DELIV = os.path.join(ROOT, "deliverables") STEM = "Tech_Inventory_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_2026-08-29" GREY = RGBColor(0x59, 0x59, 0x59) HEADER_LEFT = "BAYLOR ATHLETICS · APPLIED PERFORMANCE" HEADER_RIGHT = "INTERIM — COLLECTION OPEN TO 29 SEPTEMBER 2026" FOOTER = ("Athletics Technology Inventory · Executive Summary " "· 29 August 2026 · E. Rash") # Page geometry, shared by both renderers. MARGIN = dict(top=0.7, bottom=0.6, left=0.75, right=0.75) TEXT_WIDTH = 8.5 - MARGIN["left"] - MARGIN["right"] # 7.0 in # "Other" was an option on the form that nobody ever selected, and it looks # like a leftover from the draft list. It is not a unit that owes a response. PHANTOM_UNITS = {"Other"} # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # data # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- def figures(): def rd(name): with open(os.path.join(CLEAN, name), encoding="utf-8") as f: return list(csv.DictReader(f)) master = [r for r in rd("tech_master.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"] long = [r for r in rd("tech_inventory_long.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"] stopped = rd("stopped_using.csv") cov = [r for r in rd("coverage.csv") if r["unit"] not in PHANTOM_UNITS] units_total = len(cov) units_in = len([r for r in cov if r["status"] in ("responded", "MULTIPLE")]) outstanding = [r["unit"] for r in cov if r["status"] == "NO RESPONSE"] n_products = len(master) n_athlete = len([r for r in master if r["athlete_data_likely"] == "Y"]) n_single = len([r for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) == 1]) top = max(master, key=lambda r: int(r["unit_count"])) # One respondent wrote prose rather than a product list - a new hire still # waiting on a laptop - so submissions is one more than parsed responses. n_sub = len({r["response_id"] for r in long}) + 1 return dict( units_total=units_total, units_in=units_in, outstanding=outstanding, n_outstanding=len(outstanding), pct_units=round(100 * units_in / units_total), n_sub=n_sub, n_mentions=len(long), n_products=n_products, n_athlete=n_athlete, pct_athlete=round(100 * n_athlete / n_products), n_single=n_single, pct_single=round(100 * n_single / n_products), top_name=top["canonical"], top_units=int(top["unit_count"]), n_stopped=len(stopped), ) # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # the document, as data # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- def content(f): """Everything the reader sees. Both renderers consume this and nothing else. ** ** marks inline bold in every string. """ return dict( wordmark="BAYLOR ATHLETICS", title="Athletics Technology Inventory", subtitle="Executive Summary", meta=[ ["Status", "**Interim** — collection stays open to the department " "soft deadline of 29 September 2026"], ["Date", "August 29, 2026"], ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics"], ["Companion documents", "Athletics Technology Inventory — Findings (full report); " "Software and Technology Management Framework"], ], meta_widths=[1.55, 5.45], sections=[ dict(kind="para", tag="In brief", head="What we asked, and where it stands", body="Every unit was asked a five-question survey naming the " "technology it uses. **{units_in} of {units_total} units " "have answered so far**, describing **{n_products} " "distinct products**. Unit leaders have until 29 " "September to complete the remaining responses, so the " "figures below are an interim read rather than a final " "count.".format(**f)), dict(kind="table", tag="Coverage", head="The inventory in eight numbers", headers=["Measure", "As of 29 August 2026"], widths=[3.05, 3.95], rows=[ ["Units that have responded", "**{units_in} of {units_total}** ({pct_units}%)".format(**f)], ["Units still to respond", "**{}** — {}".format(f["n_outstanding"], ", ".join(f["outstanding"]))], ["Submissions received", "**{n_sub}**".format(**f)], ["Distinct products named", "**{n_products}**, from {n_mentions} mentions".format(**f)], ["Products that likely involve student-athlete information", "**{n_athlete}** ({pct_athlete}% of products)".format(**f)], ["Products named by one unit only", "**{n_single}** ({pct_single}% of products)".format(**f)], ["Most widely shared system", "**{top_name}**, used by {top_units} units".format(**f)], ["Products retired in the last 12 months", "**{n_stopped}**".format(**f)], ], # The full findings report counts 33 units, because that is how # many options the form carried. Saying so here keeps the two # documents from appearing to disagree when read side by side. caption="The survey list carried 33 options. One of them, " "“Other”, was never selected and is not " "counted as a unit here."), dict(kind="bullets", tag="Reading", head="Three things the numbers show", items=[ "**Most software sits with a single unit.** {n_single} of " "the {n_products} products were named by one unit only. A " "shared record of what is in use is the capability that " "makes this population visible.".format(**f), "**One system is close to department-wide.** {top_name}, " "at {top_units} units. There is no comparable second, so a " "single place to look does not exist yet — which is what " "this inventory begins to build.".format(**f), "**{n_stopped} products were retired in the last year.** " "What each vendor still holds was not asked on the short " "form, so it is not recorded anywhere yet. This is the " "smallest and most closeable gap in the dataset." .format(**f), ]), dict(kind="checklist", tag="Next", head="Checklist", headers=["", "Action", "Owner", "By"], widths=[0.28, 3.72, 1.75, 1.25], rows=[ ["", "Collect the {n_outstanding} outstanding unit " "responses.".format(**f), "Unit leaders", "29 Sept 2026"], ["", "Confirm what each vendor retained for the " "{n_stopped} retired products.".format(**f), "Applied Performance", "Oct 2026"], ["", "Compare the inventory against the ITS IDEA form " "history.", "Applied Performance / ITS", "Oct 2026"], ["", "Run the detailed review form on the {n_athlete} " "products that involve athlete information." .format(**f), "Applied Performance", "Nov 2026"], ["", "Decide how single-unit products are handled going " "forward.", "Senior staff", "Nov 2026"], ]), ], ) # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # renderer: Word # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- def kv_table(doc, rows, widths): """Label/value block. No header row - the left column holds labels, so styling it as a column heading would misread.""" t = doc.add_table(rows=0, cols=2) t.style = "Table Grid" t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT for label, value in rows: cells = t.add_row().cells shade(cells[0], "EFF2ED") p = cells[0].paragraphs[0] p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2) r = p.add_run(label) r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(8.5); r.bold = True r.font.color.rgb = MUTED p = cells[1].paragraphs[0] p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2) add_runs(p, value, size=9.5, color=INK) for row in t.rows: for i, w in enumerate(widths): row.cells[i].width = Inches(w) doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2) return t def docx_page_setup(doc): sec = doc.sections[0] sec.top_margin = Inches(MARGIN["top"]) sec.bottom_margin = Inches(MARGIN["bottom"]) sec.left_margin = Inches(MARGIN["left"]) sec.right_margin = Inches(MARGIN["right"]) hp = sec.header.paragraphs[0] hp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT r = hp.add_run(HEADER_LEFT) r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(8); r.bold = True r.font.color.rgb = GREEN r2 = hp.add_run(" " + HEADER_RIGHT) r2.font.name = BODY_FONT; r2.font.size = Pt(8); r2.bold = True r2.font.color.rgb = GOLD bottom_rule(hp) fp = sec.footer.paragraphs[0] fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT fr = fp.add_run(FOOTER + " ") fr.font.name = BODY_FONT; fr.font.size = Pt(8); fr.font.color.rgb = MUTED page_field(fp) def docx_h2(doc, tag, text): t = doc.add_paragraph() t.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(11) t.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1) r = t.add_run(tag.upper()) r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(7.5); r.bold = True r.font.color.rgb = GOLD p = doc.add_paragraph() p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0) p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6) r = p.add_run(text) r.font.name = HEAD_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(13); r.bold = True r.font.color.rgb = GREEN bottom_rule(p) def render_docx(c, out): doc = Document() style_base(doc) docx_page_setup(doc) for text, size, font, color, after in [ (c["wordmark"], 11, BODY_FONT, GREEN, 1), (c["title"], 19, HEAD_FONT, GREEN, 1), (c["subtitle"], 13, HEAD_FONT, GREY, 8), ]: p = doc.add_paragraph() p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after) r = p.add_run(text) r.font.name = font; r.font.size = Pt(size); r.bold = True r.font.color.rgb = color kv_table(doc, c["meta"], c["meta_widths"]) for s in c["sections"]: docx_h2(doc, s["tag"], s["head"]) if s["kind"] == "para": para(doc, s["body"], space_after=6) elif s["kind"] == "bullets": for item in s["items"]: p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet") p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3) add_runs(p, item, size=10) else: table(doc, s["headers"], s["rows"], widths=s["widths"]) if s.get("caption"): para(doc, s["caption"], size=8, color=MUTED, space_after=4) doc.save(out) return out # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # renderer: print twin # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- def esc(text): """Escape HTML, then turn ** ** into .""" out = (text.replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">")) parts = out.split("**") return "".join(p if i % 2 == 0 else "{}".format(p) for i, p in enumerate(parts)) def render_html(c, out): def cells(row, widths, tag="td"): return "".join( '<{t} style="width:{w}in">{v}'.format( t=tag, w=widths[i], v=esc(str(v))) for i, v in enumerate(row)) blocks = [] blocks.append( '

Cleaning and analysis of the Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory survey.

Companion to `~/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework`, which holds the framework
documents, the form specs, and the form links. This folder holds only the
collected data and what comes out of it.

## Layout

```
raw/     frozen survey exports, date-stamped. never edited.
scripts/ clean_inventory.py (parser) + aliases.py (all judgement calls)
clean/   generated CSVs. delete and regenerate freely.
docs/    findings
deliverables/  anything that goes to Kenny / Jon Allen / ITS
```

## Run

```bash
cd ~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis
uv run --with openpyxl python3 scripts/clean_inventory.py
```

The script reads the newest `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx` and rewrites
everything in `clean/`. It is safe to run repeatedly.

## Refresh with a newer export

1. Download the responses from Microsoft Forms.
2. Save as `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx`.
3. Re-run the command above.
4. Check `clean/unmapped_review.csv`. If it has rows, add them to
   `scripts/aliases.py` and run again. It should end empty.

## Outputs

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `clean/tech_inventory_long.csv` | one row per unit × technology |
| `clean/tech_master.csv` | one row per distinct technology, with unit count |
| `clean/coverage.csv` | which of the 26 units responded, missed, or answered twice |
| `clean/stopped_using.csv` | technology retired in the last 12 months |
| `clean/unmapped_review.csv` | strings the alias map did not recognise |
| `clean/prose_responses_review.csv` | answers that were prose, not a list |

## Ground rules

- **Nothing is guessed silently.** Unrecognised names go to
  `unmapped_review.csv` rather than being auto-matched.
- **All name merging lives in `scripts/aliases.py`.** The parser is mechanical.
- `raw/` is never modified. Re-analysis always starts from the frozen export.
- The export carries respondent names and email addresses. Strip those before
  anything is shared or published.

## Two things Microsoft Forms does that will bite you

1. **The export declares a bogus sheet size** (`A1:A1`). openpyxl's fast
   `read_only` reader trusts it and returns an empty sheet. The script loads
   the workbook normally instead. Do not "optimise" that back.
2. **The system columns move between exports.** The 2026-08-29 export added a
   "Last modified time" column and shifted every question one place right.
   The script finds columns by header text, never by position.

## Status

Done against the post-deadline **2026-08-29** export: 37 responses, 27 of 34
units, 147 distinct technologies. See `docs/FINDINGS_2026-08-29.md`.

The 2026-08-24 export (15 responses) is kept in `raw/` for comparison. The
script always uses the newest file.

**What to do:** forward the PDF freely. Open the .docx in Word once before you send that version.

**2. Some dates and owners are mine, not agreed.** Row 1 (unit leaders, 29 Sept) comes from the all-staff meeting. The Oct/Nov dates and "Senior staff" are my suggestion. Change them before it goes out.

**3. One number differs from the big report on purpose.** The one-pager says 27 of **32** units. The full report says 33. The 33rd is "Other", a leftover form option nobody picked. There is a small note on the page explaining it, so the two documents do not look like they disagree.

p="scripts/build_exec_summary.py"

new_main = '''def chrome_pdf(html_path, pdf_path):
    chrome = "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome"
    subprocess.run(
        [chrome, "--headless", "--disable-gpu", "--no-pdf-header-footer",
         "--print-to-pdf=" + pdf_path, "file://" + html_path],
        check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
    return pdf_path


def word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path):
    """Export through Word and ask it how many pages it laid out.

    Word is the authority here: it is what the reader opens, and its layout is
    measurably taller than the HTML twin's - tables and list styles carry
    spacing the twin does not reproduce. Returns the page count, or None when
    Word cannot be driven (it blocks on a dialog if the app is not already
    open, so this is best-effort by design).
    """
    script = \'\'\'
    tell application "Microsoft Word"
      open POSIX file "{docx}"
      set d to active document
      set n to (compute statistics d statistic statistic pages)
      save as d file name POSIX file "{pdf}" file format format PDF
      close d saving no
      return n
    end tell
    \'\'\'.format(docx=docx_path, pdf=pdf_path)
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["osascript", "-e", script],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=90)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return None
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return None
    try:
        return int(r.stdout.strip())
    except ValueError:
        return None


def page_count(pdf_path):
    import pypdfium2 as pdfium
    return len(pdfium.PdfDocument(pdf_path))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main():
    c = content(figures())

    docx_path = os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".docx")
    html_path = os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".html")
    pdf_path = os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".pdf")

    render_docx(c, docx_path)
    print("wrote", docx_path)

    render_html(c, html_path)

    n = word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path)
    if n is not None:
        source = "Word"
        print("wrote", pdf_path, "(from Word) ->", n, "page(s)")
    else:
        # Word would not answer - it needs the app already open, and blocks on
        # an invisible dialog otherwise. Fall back to the twin and say so.
        chrome_pdf(html_path, pdf_path)
        n = page_count(pdf_path)
        source = "the HTML twin"
        print("wrote", pdf_path, "(from the HTML twin) ->", n, "page(s)")
        print("[warn] Word did not answer, so the page count is the twin's, "
              "not Word's. Open Microsoft Word and re-run to confirm.")

    if n != 1:
        sys.exit("[error] the executive summary must fit one page; {} laid out "
                 "{}. Cut a checklist row or a bullet.".format(source, n))
    print("one page confirmed by", source)


if __name__ == "__main__":
