# Tech_Inventory_Analysis

Cleaning and analysis of the Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory survey.

Companion to `~/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework`, which holds the framework
documents, the form specs, and the form links. This folder holds only the
collected data and what comes out of it.

## Layout

```
raw/     frozen survey exports, date-stamped. never edited.
scripts/ clean_inventory.py (parser) + aliases.py (all judgement calls)
clean/   generated CSVs. delete and regenerate freely.
docs/    findings
deliverables/  anything that goes to Kenny / Jon Allen / ITS
```

## Run

```bash
cd ~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis
uv run --with openpyxl python3 scripts/clean_inventory.py
```

The script reads the newest `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx` and rewrites
everything in `clean/`. It is safe to run repeatedly.

Then rebuild the two documents. Both read `clean/*.csv`, so neither can drift
from the data:

```bash
uv run --with python-docx python3 scripts/build_docx.py
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_exec_summary.py
```

`build_exec_summary.py` writes the `.docx` and, from the same content model, a
print twin that headless Chrome renders to `.pdf`. It counts the pages and
**fails the build if the summary spills past one page** — that is the point of
the document, so it is enforced rather than trusted. Word on this machine will
not accept AppleScript automation from a non-interactive session, which is why
the PDF comes from Chrome rather than from Word.

## Refresh with a newer export

1. Download the responses from Microsoft Forms.
2. Save as `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx`.
3. Re-run the command above.
4. Check `clean/unmapped_review.csv`. If it has rows, add them to
   `scripts/aliases.py` and run again. It should end empty.

## Outputs

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `clean/tech_inventory_long.csv` | one row per unit × technology |
| `clean/tech_master.csv` | one row per distinct technology, with unit count |
| `clean/coverage.csv` | which of the 26 units responded, missed, or answered twice |
| `clean/stopped_using.csv` | technology retired in the last 12 months |
| `clean/unmapped_review.csv` | strings the alias map did not recognise |
| `clean/prose_responses_review.csv` | answers that were prose, not a list |
| `deliverables/Tech_Inventory_FINDINGS_ER_*.docx` / `.pdf` / `.html` | the full findings report — the working document |
| `deliverables/Tech_Inventory_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_*.docx` / `.pdf` | the one-page summary — the document that gets forwarded |

Published copies of the deliverables live in OneDrive under
`00_Primary_Storage_Drive/05_SYSTEMS/SoftwareTechDocs/TechInventory_2026-08/`.
`raw/*.xlsx` is never copied there: it carries respondent names and emails.

## Ground rules

- **Nothing is guessed silently.** Unrecognised names go to
  `unmapped_review.csv` rather than being auto-matched.
- **All name merging lives in `scripts/aliases.py`.** The parser is mechanical.
- `raw/` is never modified. Re-analysis always starts from the frozen export.
- The export carries respondent names and email addresses. Strip those before
  anything is shared or published.

## Two things Microsoft Forms does that will bite you

1. **The export declares a bogus sheet size** (`A1:A1`). openpyxl's fast
   `read_only` reader trusts it and returns an empty sheet. The script loads
   the workbook normally instead. Do not "optimise" that back.
2. **The system columns move between exports.** The 2026-08-29 export added a
   "Last modified time" column and shifted every question one place right.
   The script finds columns by header text, never by position.

## Status

Done against the post-deadline **2026-08-29** export: 37 responses, 27 of 34
units, 147 distinct technologies. See `docs/FINDINGS_2026-08-29.md`.

The 2026-08-24 export (15 responses) is kept in `raw/` for comparison. The
script always uses the newest file.

content.text:
Fixed and verified. Here's what happened.

## You were right to open Word

**The .docx really was two pages.** My stand-in check said one page. Word said two. The stand-in was wrong.

Word only answers when the app is already open. Before, it froze silently on a hidden pop-up.

## What I changed

The tables had a blank line after each one, plus 2 points of padding in every cell. On a one-page document that adds up to about one and a half checklist rows. I removed both.

Then I made **Word itself the checker**. The build now:
1. Writes the .docx
2. Asks Word to lay it out and count pages
3. Exports the PDF **from Word**, so the two files match exactly
4. **Stops with an error if Word says more than one page**

Result: **one page, confirmed by Word.** I looked at Word's own render — clean, nothing cut off, space to spare at the bottom.

## Files (updated in both places)

```
~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis/deliverables/Tech_Inventory_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_2026-08-29.docx
~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis/deliverables/Tech_Inventory_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_2026-08-29.pdf
```

OneDrive copies re-synced, checksums match. No respondent names or emails in either file.

## To rebuild later

**Open Word first**, then:

```
cd ~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_exec_summary.py
```

If Word is closed it warns you and its answer should not be trusted. That warning is now in the README too.

## Still your call

The dates in rows 2–5 (Oct 2026, Nov 2026) and "Senior staff" as an owner are **my suggestions**, not anything agreed. Row 1 (unit leaders, 29 Sept) comes from the all-staff meeting. Change the rest before you send it.

Want me to save the "open Word first" quirk to memory? It will bite again on any future Word job.

content.content:
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# document
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main():
    master, long, cov, stopped, unmapped = load()

    n_resp = len({r["response_id"] for r in long}) + 1   # + the prose response
    units_total = len(cov)
    units_in = len([r for r in cov if r["status"] in ("responded", "MULTIPLE")])
    units_out = [r["unit"] for r in cov if r["status"] == "NO RESPONSE"
                 and r["unit"] != "Other"]
    n_products = len(master)
    n_athlete = len([r for r in master if r["athlete_data_likely"] == "Y"])
    n_single = len([r for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) == 1])
    n_mentions = len(long)

    doc = Document()
    style_base(doc)
    build_header_footer(doc)

    # --- title -----------------------------------------------------------
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    r = p.add_run("TECHNOLOGY INVENTORY")
    r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(8); r.bold = True
    r.font.color.rgb = GOLD

    h1(doc, "Athletics Technology Inventory")
    para(doc,
         "Thirty-seven departments answered five questions about the software "
         "they run. The answer is not that there is too much technology. It is "
         "that almost none of it is shared.",
         size=12, color=RGBColor(0x37, 0x47, 0x3F), space_after=10,
         font=HEAD_FONT)

    table(doc, ["Reported", "Source", "Status"],
          [["29 August 2026",
            "Microsoft Forms — Quick Inventory (5 questions)",
            "Interim; department soft deadline 29 September 2026"]],
          widths=[1.3, 2.9, 2.5])

    # --- headline figures -------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "At a glance", "Where the inventory stands")
    table(doc,
          ["Measure", "Figure", "Note"],
          [["Submissions to date", n_resp,
            "36 listed technology; one was a new hire awaiting equipment"],
           ["Units responding", "{} of {}".format(units_in, units_total),
            "Interim — five units still outstanding, one month to run"],
           ["Distinct products", n_products,
            "Resolved from {} separate mentions".format(n_mentions)],
           ["Products touching athlete data", n_athlete,
            "{}% of the estate, by category — a screening list, not a "
            "confirmed count".format(round(100 * n_athlete / n_products))],
           ["Products used by a single unit", n_single,
            "{}% of the estate".format(round(100 * n_single / n_products))]],
          widths=[2.1, 0.9, 3.7], numeric_cols=(1,))

    # --- coverage ---------------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "Coverage", "Who has responded")
    para(doc,
         "Twenty-seven of thirty-three units have responded so far. Five are "
         "still outstanding, and one of them holds the contract records.")

    para(doc, "**Two deadlines, not one.** 29 August was Applied Performance's "
              "own deadline. The all-staff meeting on 24 August set a "
              "department-wide soft deadline of **29 September**, with unit "
              "leaders assigning staff to complete it. Every figure in this "
              "document is an interim read at the earlier date.",
         space_before=4)

    h3(doc, "Still outstanding")
    para(doc, "  ·  ".join(units_out), bold=True, space_after=4)
    para(doc, "The Business Office is the one worth a direct ask. It holds the "
              "contract records this inventory is designed to be read against.")

    h3(doc, "Units that submitted more than once")
    multi = [(r["unit"], r["responses"]) for r in cov if r["status"] == "MULTIPLE"]
    para(doc, ", ".join("{} ({})".format(u, n) for u, n in multi) + ".",
         space_after=4)
    para(doc, "These are different people describing different slices of the "
              "same unit. They are kept and tagged rather than merged.")

    h3(doc, "The unit list differs from the original form spec")
    para(doc,
         "The live Microsoft Form offers units the written spec does not, and "
         "spells two of them differently — which is why Track & Field / Cross "
         "Country and Acrobatics & Tumbling initially appeared as "
         "non-responses. Those spellings are reconciled here. The working list "
         "is {} units and is worth confirming against the live form."
         .format(units_total))

    doc.add_page_break()

    # --- coverage table ---------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "Coverage detail", "Response count by unit")
    rows = []
    for r in cov:
        n = int(r["responses"])
        label = ("Not yet in" if n == 0 else
                 "Responded" if n == 1 else "{} people".format(n))
        rows.append([r["unit"], n, label])
    table(doc, ["Unit", "Responses", "Status"], rows,
          widths=[3.4, 1.0, 2.3], numeric_cols=(1,))

    doc.add_page_break()

    # --- the estate -------------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "The estate", "Three quarters of it is used by exactly one unit")
    para(doc,
         "{} of {} products were named by a single unit. That long tail — not "
         "the vendor overlap — is the finding. It is the population no central "
         "process currently sees."
         .format(n_single, n_products))
    para(doc,
         "It includes AI tools adopted locally (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, "
         "Microsoft Copilot), a scatter of productivity apps (Notion, Asana, "
         "Todoist, Padlet, Sling, GroupMe, WhatsApp, TeamUp), and one-off "
         "athlete-facing systems (Nix Biosensors, Calera CORE, Boost "
         "Treadmills, C3 Logix, XO Armor, Hologic DXA).")

    h3(doc, "Distinct products by category")
    cats = {}
    for r in master:
        cats[r["category"]] = cats.get(r["category"], 0) + 1
    pretty = {"video-analytics": "Video & analytics", "comms-media": "Comms & media",
              "office-general": "Office general", "equipment-ops": "Equipment ops",
              "athlete-management": "Athlete management", "ai-general": "AI tools",
              "food-travel": "Food & travel", "social-media": "Social media",
              "athlete-stipend": "Athlete stipend", "uncategorised": "Unidentified"}
    crows = [[pretty.get(k, k.capitalize()), v]
             for k, v in sorted(cats.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])]
    table(doc, ["Category", "Products"], crows,
          widths=[3.0, 1.0], numeric_cols=(1,))

    h3(doc, "Products used by three or more units")
    srows = [[r["canonical"], int(r["unit_count"]),
              pretty.get(r["category"], r["category"].capitalize())]
             for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) >= 3]
    table(doc, ["Product", "Units", "Category"], srows,
          widths=[2.6, 0.9, 2.2], numeric_cols=(1,))
    para(doc, "**Teamworks, at twelve units, is the only thing close to a "
              "department-wide system.** Everything below it is departmental "
              "at best.", space_before=3)

    # --- overlap ----------------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "Overlap", "Four vendors, one job")
    para(doc, "The consolidation conversation is now answerable with counts "
              "rather than estimates.")
    table(doc, ["Job", "Vendors in use"],
          [["Athlete tracking",
            "Catapult (6 units), Kinexon (3), Polar (1); Firstbeat arriving"],
           ["Force & speed testing", "VALD (6), Perch (3), GymAware, TMG"],
           ["Athlete management", "Teamworks (12), Kitman Labs (6), XPS Network"],
           ["Video & analytics",
            "Hudl, DVSport, Synergy, Spiideo, Kinovea and 14 more"]],
          widths=[1.9, 4.8])

    doc.add_page_break()

    # --- exposure ---------------------------------------------------------
    h2(doc, "Open items", "Seven products retired, no recorded data disposition")
    para(doc,
         "Every retirement in the last twelve months left athlete data "
         "somewhere. The short form did not ask where, so the answer is simply "
         "not captured anywhere yet. Confirming what each vendor retained is "
         "the most concrete, closeable action in this dataset.")
    table(doc, ["Unit", "Product", "Vendor retention"],
          [[r["unit"], r["canonical"], "Not asked"] for r in stopped],
          widths=[2.3, 2.3, 2.1])

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Baylor Athletics house style for Word documents.

One module, imported by every document builder, so the look is defined once.

    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style")
    from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc

    d = BaylorDoc("Athletics Technology Inventory",
                  deck="What the department runs, and who runs it.",
                  status="Interim - collection open to 29 September 2026")
    d.meta([["Status", "Interim"], ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance"]])
    d.callout("How to read this", "Every figure is an interim read.")
    d.section("Coverage")
    d.para("Twenty-seven of thirty-two units have responded.")
    d.table(["Unit", "Responses"], [["Football", 3]])
    d.save("out.docx")

WHERE THE STYLE COMES FROM
--------------------------
Every measurement here was read out of
    SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/deliverables/
        Software_and_Technology_Management_Framework_DRAFT.docx
which Eric chose on 2026-08-30 as the house look. Nothing is invented. If the
exemplar and this module ever disagree, the exemplar wins - re-measure it
rather than adjusting to taste.

TWO THINGS NOT TO "IMPROVE"
---------------------------
Calibri, everywhere. The exemplar sets no font on any run, so every size
inherits Normal. Calibri ships with Office, which is why the document survives
being emailed. Baylor's licensed faces live in ~/DEV/Baylor_Fonts, but a
document set in them renders as a fallback on any machine that lacks them.

No running header. The exemplar has an empty header and carries the document's
status in the meta block and the footer instead. That still puts the status on
every page, which is the constraint that matters.

INLINE BOLD
-----------
Every text argument accepts ``**like this**`` for inline bold.
"""

from docx import Document
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor

__all__ = ["BaylorDoc", "GREEN", "GOLD", "GREY", "CREAM", "INK", "BODY_FONT"]

# --- palette, straight from the exemplar ---------------------------------
GREEN = RGBColor(0x15, 0x47, 0x34)      # Baylor green: titles, headings, rules
GOLD = RGBColor(0xB8, 0x86, 0x0B)       # the eyebrow line only
GREY = RGBColor(0x59, 0x59, 0x59)       # decks, notes, the footer
CREAM = "FFF4DA"                        # callout fill
WHITE = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)      # text on a green table header
INK = None                              # body text: Word's default, not black

BODY_FONT = "Calibri"

# --- page and base paragraph ---------------------------------------------
MARGIN = dict(top=0.80, bottom=0.80, left=0.90, right=0.90)
BODY_SIZE = 10.5
BODY_AFTER = 6
LINE_SPACING = 1.0791666666666666       # the exemplar's exact value

EYEBROW_DEFAULT = "BAYLOR ATHLETICS  ·  APPLIED PERFORMANCE"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# low-level helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def add_runs(p, text, size=BODY_SIZE, bold=False, italic=False, color=INK,
             font=BODY_FONT):
    """Add text to a paragraph, splitting on ** ** for inline bold."""
    for i, chunk in enumerate(str(text).split("**")):
        if not chunk:
            continue
        r = p.add_run(chunk)
        r.font.name = font
        r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if color is not None:
            r.font.color.rgb = color
        r.bold = bold or (i % 2 == 1)
        r.italic = italic
    return p


def bottom_rule(p, color="154734", size=6):
    """The hairline under a section heading."""
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    bd = OxmlElement("w:pBdr")
    b = OxmlElement("w:bottom")
    b.set(qn("w:val"), "single")
    b.set(qn("w:sz"), str(size))
    b.set(qn("w:space"), "3")
    b.set(qn("w:color"), color)
    bd.append(b)
    pPr.append(bd)


def shade(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    sh = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    sh.set(qn("w:val"), "clear")
    sh.set(qn("w:fill"), hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(sh)


def page_field(p, size=7.5, color=GREY):
    """PAGE of NUMPAGES, as real Word fields rather than baked-in numbers."""
    def fld(instr):
        r = OxmlElement("w:r")
        b = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); b.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "begin")
        i = OxmlElement("w:instrText"); i.set(qn("xml:space"), "preserve")
        i.text = instr
        e = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); e.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "end")
        r.append(b); r.append(i); r.append(e)
        return r
    for txt, instr in (("", "PAGE"), (" of ", "NUMPAGES")):
        if txt:
            run = p.add_run(txt)
            run.font.size = Pt(size); run.font.color.rgb = color
            run.font.name = BODY_FONT
        p._p.append(fld(instr))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
class BaylorDoc:
    """A Word document in the house style.

    Call the content methods in reading order and then save(). Section numbers
    are handed out automatically, so inserting a section never means renumbering
    the ones after it.
    """

    def __init__(self, title, deck=None, status=None,
                 eyebrow=EYEBROW_DEFAULT, footer_suffix="Baylor Athletics",
                 page_numbers=True):
        self.doc = Document()
        self.title = title
        self.status = status
        self._section_no = 0
        self._base_style()
        self._page_setup()
        self._footer(footer_suffix, page_numbers)
        self._title_block(title, deck, eyebrow)

    # -- setup -------------------------------------------------------------
    def _base_style(self):
        st = self.doc.styles["Normal"]
        st.font.name = BODY_FONT
        st.font.size = Pt(BODY_SIZE)
        st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(BODY_AFTER)
        st.paragraph_format.line_spacing = LINE_SPACING

    def _page_setup(self):
        sec = self.doc.sections[0]
        sec.top_margin = Inches(MARGIN["top"])
        sec.bottom_margin = Inches(MARGIN["bottom"])
        sec.left_margin = Inches(MARGIN["left"])
        sec.right_margin = Inches(MARGIN["right"])
        self.text_width = 8.5 - MARGIN["left"] - MARGIN["right"]

    def _footer(self, suffix, page_numbers):
        """Centred, quiet, and carrying the document's status on every page."""
        fp = self.doc.sections[0].footer.paragraphs[0]
        fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        parts = [self.title]
        if self.status:
            parts.append(self.status)
        parts.append(suffix)
        r = fp.add_run("   ·   ".join(parts))
        r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(7.5); r.font.color.rgb = GREY
        if page_numbers:
            r2 = fp.add_run("   ·   ")
            r2.font.name = BODY_FONT; r2.font.size = Pt(7.5)
            r2.font.color.rgb = GREY
            page_field(fp)

    def _title_block(self, title, deck, eyebrow):
        if eyebrow:
            p = self._p(space_after=1)
            add_runs(p, eyebrow, size=9, bold=True, color=GOLD)
        p = self._p(space_after=2)
        add_runs(p, title, size=19, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        if deck:
            p = self._p(space_after=10)
            add_runs(p, deck, size=11, italic=True, color=GREY)

    def _p(self, space_before=None, space_after=None, style=None):
        p = self.doc.add_paragraph(style=style) if style else self.doc.add_paragraph()
        if space_before is not None:
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(space_before)
        if space_after is not None:
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
        return p

    # -- content -----------------------------------------------------------
    def meta(self, rows, label_width=1.5):
        """The status block under the title. Borderless: it is a label/value
        list that happens to be laid out in a table, not a data table."""
        t = self.doc.add_table(rows=0, cols=2)
        t.style = "Normal Table"
        t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
        for label, value in rows:
            cells = t.add_row().cells
            p = cells[0].paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            add_runs(p, label, size=9, bold=True)
            p = cells[1].paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            add_runs(p, value, size=9)
        for row in t.rows:
            row.cells[0].width = Inches(label_width)
            row.cells[1].width = Inches(self.text_width - label_width)
        self._p(space_after=4)
        return t

    def callout(self, head, body):
        """The cream box. For how to read the document, or a caveat that has to
        be seen before the reader starts."""
        t = self.doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=1)
        t.style = "Table Grid"
        cell = t.rows[0].cells[0]
        shade(cell, CREAM)
        p = cell.paragraphs[0]
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
        add_runs(p, head, size=9.5, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        p = cell.add_paragraph()
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
        add_runs(p, body, size=9.5)
        cell.width = Inches(self.text_width)
        self._p(space_after=4)
        return t

    def section(self, text, numbered=True):
        """A top-level heading, numbered in sequence and underlined in green."""
        if numbered:
            self._section_no += 1
            text = "{}.  {}".format(self._section_no, text)
        p = self._p(space_before=14, space_after=5)
        add_runs(p, text, size=13, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        bottom_rule(p)
        return p

    def subhead(self, text):
        p = self._p(space_before=10, space_after=3)
        add_runs(p, text, size=11.5, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        return p

    def para(self, text, space_before=None, space_after=BODY_AFTER):
        p = self._p(space_before=space_before, space_after=space_after)
        return add_runs(p, text)

    def note(self, text):
        """Small italic grey. A caveat that belongs beside the thing it
        qualifies rather than in a callout."""
        p = self._p(space_after=BODY_AFTER)
        return add_runs(p, text, size=9.5, italic=True, color=GREY)

    def small(self, text):
        """Small plain grey. A caption under a table."""
        p = self._p(space_after=BODY_AFTER)
        return add_runs(p, text, size=9.5, color=GREY)

    def bullets(self, items):
        for item in items:
            p = self.doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet")
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.4)
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.19)
            add_runs(p, item)

    def numbered(self, items):
        """A hanging numbered list. Used for recommended actions, where the
        number is referred to in conversation."""
        for i, item in enumerate(items, start=1):
            p = self._p(space_after=BODY_AFTER)
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.28)
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.28)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Baylor Athletics house style for Word documents.

One module, imported by every document builder, so the look is defined once.

    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style")
    from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc

    d = BaylorDoc("Athletics Technology Inventory",
                  deck="What the department runs, and who runs it.",
                  status="Interim - collection open to 29 September 2026")
    d.meta([["Status", "Interim"], ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance"]])
    d.callout("How to read this", "Every figure is an interim read.")
    d.section("Coverage")
    d.para("Twenty-seven of thirty-two units have responded.")
    d.table(["Unit", "Responses"], [["Football", 3]])
    d.save("out.docx")

WHERE THE STYLE COMES FROM
--------------------------
Every measurement here was read out of
    SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/deliverables/
        Software_and_Technology_Management_Framework_DRAFT.docx
which Eric chose on 2026-08-30 as the house look. Nothing is invented. If the
exemplar and this module ever disagree, the exemplar wins - re-measure it
rather than adjusting to taste.

TWO THINGS NOT TO "IMPROVE"
---------------------------
Calibri, everywhere. The exemplar sets no font on any run, so every size
inherits Normal. Calibri ships with Office, which is why the document survives
being emailed. Baylor's licensed faces live in ~/DEV/Baylor_Fonts, but a
document set in them renders as a fallback on any machine that lacks them.

No running header. The exemplar has an empty header and carries the document's
status in the meta block and the footer instead. That still puts the status on
every page, which is the constraint that matters.

INLINE BOLD
-----------
Every text argument accepts ``**like this**`` for inline bold.
"""

from docx import Document
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor

__all__ = ["BaylorDoc", "GREEN", "GOLD", "GREY", "CREAM", "INK", "BODY_FONT"]

# --- palette, straight from the exemplar ---------------------------------
GREEN = RGBColor(0x15, 0x47, 0x34)      # Baylor green: titles, headings, rules
GOLD = RGBColor(0xB8, 0x86, 0x0B)       # the eyebrow line only
GREY = RGBColor(0x59, 0x59, 0x59)       # decks, notes, the footer
CREAM = "FFF4DA"                        # callout fill
WHITE = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)      # text on a green table header
INK = None                              # body text: Word's default, not black

BODY_FONT = "Calibri"

# --- page and base paragraph ---------------------------------------------
MARGIN = dict(top=0.80, bottom=0.80, left=0.90, right=0.90)
BODY_SIZE = 10.5
BODY_AFTER = 6
LINE_SPACING = 1.0791666666666666       # the exemplar's exact value

EYEBROW_DEFAULT = "BAYLOR ATHLETICS  ·  APPLIED PERFORMANCE"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# low-level helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def add_runs(p, text, size=BODY_SIZE, bold=False, italic=False, color=INK,
             font=BODY_FONT):
    """Add text to a paragraph, splitting on ** ** for inline bold."""
    for i, chunk in enumerate(str(text).split("**")):
        if not chunk:
            continue
        r = p.add_run(chunk)
        r.font.name = font
        r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if color is not None:
            r.font.color.rgb = color
        r.bold = bold or (i % 2 == 1)
        r.italic = italic
    return p


def bottom_rule(p, color="154734", size=6):
    """The hairline under a section heading."""
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    bd = OxmlElement("w:pBdr")
    b = OxmlElement("w:bottom")
    b.set(qn("w:val"), "single")
    b.set(qn("w:sz"), str(size))
    b.set(qn("w:space"), "3")
    b.set(qn("w:color"), color)
    bd.append(b)
    pPr.append(bd)


def shade(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    sh = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    sh.set(qn("w:val"), "clear")
    sh.set(qn("w:fill"), hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(sh)


def page_field(p, size=7.5, color=GREY):
    """PAGE of NUMPAGES, as real Word fields rather than baked-in numbers."""
    def fld(instr):
        r = OxmlElement("w:r")
        b = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); b.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "begin")
        i = OxmlElement("w:instrText"); i.set(qn("xml:space"), "preserve")
        i.text = instr
        e = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); e.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "end")
        r.append(b); r.append(i); r.append(e)
        return r
    for txt, instr in (("", "PAGE"), (" of ", "NUMPAGES")):
        if txt:
            run = p.add_run(txt)
            run.font.size = Pt(size); run.font.color.rgb = color
            run.font.name = BODY_FONT
        p._p.append(fld(instr))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
class BaylorDoc:
    """A Word document in the house style.

    Call the content methods in reading order and then save(). Section numbers
    are handed out automatically, so inserting a section never means renumbering
    the ones after it.
    """

    def __init__(self, title, deck=None, status=None,
                 eyebrow=EYEBROW_DEFAULT, footer_suffix="Baylor Athletics",
                 page_numbers=True):
        self.doc = Document()
        self.title = title
        self.status = status
        self._section_no = 0
        self._base_style()
        self._page_setup()
        self._footer(footer_suffix, page_numbers)
        self._title_block(title, deck, eyebrow)

    # -- setup -------------------------------------------------------------
    def _base_style(self):
        st = self.doc.styles["Normal"]
        st.font.name = BODY_FONT
        st.font.size = Pt(BODY_SIZE)
        st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(BODY_AFTER)
        st.paragraph_format.line_spacing = LINE_SPACING

    def _page_setup(self):
        sec = self.doc.sections[0]
        sec.top_margin = Inches(MARGIN["top"])
        sec.bottom_margin = Inches(MARGIN["bottom"])
        sec.left_margin = Inches(MARGIN["left"])
        sec.right_margin = Inches(MARGIN["right"])
        self.text_width = 8.5 - MARGIN["left"] - MARGIN["right"]

    def _footer(self, suffix, page_numbers):
        """Centred, quiet, and carrying the document's status on every page."""
        fp = self.doc.sections[0].footer.paragraphs[0]
        fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        parts = [self.title]
        if self.status:
            parts.append(self.status)
        parts.append(suffix)
        r = fp.add_run("   ·   ".join(parts))
        r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(7.5); r.font.color.rgb = GREY
        if page_numbers:
            r2 = fp.add_run("   ·   ")
            r2.font.name = BODY_FONT; r2.font.size = Pt(7.5)
            r2.font.color.rgb = GREY
            page_field(fp)

    def _title_block(self, title, deck, eyebrow):
        if eyebrow:
            p = self._p(space_after=1)
            add_runs(p, eyebrow, size=9, bold=True, color=GOLD)
        p = self._p(space_after=2)
        add_runs(p, title, size=19, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        if deck:
            p = self._p(space_after=10)
            add_runs(p, deck, size=11, italic=True, color=GREY)

    def _p(self, space_before=None, space_after=None, style=None):
        p = self.doc.add_paragraph(style=style) if style else self.doc.add_paragraph()
        if space_before is not None:
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(space_before)
        if space_after is not None:
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
        return p

    # -- content -----------------------------------------------------------
    def meta(self, rows, label_width=1.5):
        """The status block under the title. Borderless: it is a label/value
        list that happens to be laid out in a table, not a data table."""
        t = self.doc.add_table(rows=0, cols=2)
        t.style = "Normal Table"
        t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
        for label, value in rows:
            cells = t.add_row().cells
            p = cells[0].paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            add_runs(p, label, size=9, bold=True)
            p = cells[1].paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            add_runs(p, value, size=9)
        for row in t.rows:
            row.cells[0].width = Inches(label_width)
            row.cells[1].width = Inches(self.text_width - label_width)
        self._p(space_after=4)
        return t

    def callout(self, head, body):
        """The cream box. For how to read the document, or a caveat that has to
        be seen before the reader starts."""
        t = self.doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=1)
        t.style = "Table Grid"
        cell = t.rows[0].cells[0]
        shade(cell, CREAM)
        p = cell.paragraphs[0]
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
        add_runs(p, head, size=9.5, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        p = cell.add_paragraph()
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
        add_runs(p, body, size=9.5)
        cell.width = Inches(self.text_width)
        self._p(space_after=4)
        return t

    def section(self, text, numbered=True):
        """A top-level heading, numbered in sequence and underlined in green."""
        if numbered:
            self._section_no += 1
            text = "{}.  {}".format(self._section_no, text)
        p = self._p(space_before=14, space_after=5)
        add_runs(p, text, size=13, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        bottom_rule(p)
        return p

    def subhead(self, text):
        p = self._p(space_before=10, space_after=3)
        add_runs(p, text, size=11.5, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        return p

    def para(self, text, space_before=None, space_after=BODY_AFTER):
        p = self._p(space_before=space_before, space_after=space_after)
        return add_runs(p, text)

    def note(self, text):
        """Small italic grey. A caveat that belongs beside the thing it
        qualifies rather than in a callout."""
        p = self._p(space_after=BODY_AFTER)
        return add_runs(p, text, size=9.5, italic=True, color=GREY)

    def small(self, text):
        """Small plain grey. A caption under a table."""
        p = self._p(space_after=BODY_AFTER)
        return add_runs(p, text, size=9.5, color=GREY)

    def bullets(self, items):
        for item in items:
            p = self.doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet")
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.4)
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.19)
            add_runs(p, item)

    def numbered(self, items):
        """A hanging numbered list. Used for recommended actions, where the
        number is referred to in conversation."""
        for i, item in enumerate(items, start=1):
            p = self._p(space_after=BODY_AFTER)
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.28)
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.28)
            r = p.add_run("{}.  ".format(i))
            r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(BODY_SIZE)
            r.bold = True; r.font.color.rgb = GOLD
            add_runs(p, item)

    def quote(self, text):
        """A pulled quotation, indented and set in green italic."""
        p = self._p(space_after=BODY_AFTER)
        p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.3)
        return add_runs(p, "“{}”".format(text.strip("“”\"")),
                        size=11.5, italic=True, color=GREEN)

    def table(self, headers, rows, widths=None, numeric_cols=(),
              caption=None, compact=False):
        """A data table: green header band, white header text, thin grid."""
        t = self.doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
        t.style = "Table Grid"
        t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
        pad = 0 if compact else 2
        for i, htext in enumerate(headers):
            cell = t.rows[0].cells[i]
            shade(cell, "154734")
            p = cell.paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(pad)
            if i in numeric_cols:
                p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
            add_runs(p, htext, size=9.5, bold=True, color=WHITE)
        for row in rows:
            cells = t.add_row().cells
            for i, val in enumerate(row):
                p = cells[i].paragraphs[0]
                p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(pad)
                if i in numeric_cols:
                    p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
                add_runs(p, val, size=9.5)
        if widths:
            for row in t.rows:
                for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                    row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
        if not compact:
            self._p(space_after=2)
        if caption:
            self.small(caption)
        return t

    def page_break(self):
        self.doc.add_page_break()

    def spacer(self, points=4):
        self._p(space_after=points)

    # -- output ------------------------------------------------------------
    def save(self, path):
        self.doc.save(path)
        return path

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the full findings report for the technology inventory.

Run (open Microsoft Word first, so the PDF can be exported from the .docx):
    uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_docx.py

This is the analyst's working document - the long one. The one-page executive
summary that gets forwarded is built by scripts/build_exec_summary.py.

Every table is read from clean/*.csv so the document cannot drift from the
data. Prose lives here rather than being parsed out of the HTML report, because
the two formats want different phrasing.

The look comes from ~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style, which is measured from
Software_and_Technology_Management_Framework_DRAFT.docx - the house style Eric
chose on 2026-08-30. Do not restyle this file directly; change the module.

House rules from Kenny Boyd's review history still apply:
  - Document status visible on every page. The house style carries it in the
    footer and the meta block rather than a running header.
  - No language implying the department was previously incompetent. Findings
    are written as capability the framework would add, not as failure.
  - Neutral, descriptive labels. Nothing that ranks a unit.
"""

import csv
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style")
from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
CLEAN = os.path.join(ROOT, "clean")
DELIV = os.path.join(ROOT, "deliverables")
STEM = "Tech_Inventory_FINDINGS_ER_2026-08-29"

TITLE = "Athletics Technology Inventory"
DECK = ("Thirty-seven submissions across the department. The finding is not "
        "that there is too much technology — it is that almost none of it is "
        "shared.")
STATUS = "Interim — collection open to 29 September 2026"

PRETTY = {"video-analytics": "Video & analytics", "comms-media": "Comms & media",
          "office-general": "Office general", "equipment-ops": "Equipment ops",
          "athlete-management": "Athlete management", "ai-general": "AI tools",
          "food-travel": "Food & travel", "social-media": "Social media",
          "athlete-stipend": "Athlete stipend", "uncategorised": "Unidentified"}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# data
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load():
    def rd(name):
        with open(os.path.join(CLEAN, name), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return list(csv.DictReader(f))

    master = [r for r in rd("tech_master.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    long = [r for r in rd("tech_inventory_long.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    return (master, long, rd("coverage.csv"), rd("stopped_using.csv"),
            rd("unmapped_review.csv"))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main():
    master, long, cov, stopped, unmapped = load()

    n_resp = len({r["response_id"] for r in long}) + 1   # + the prose response
    units_total = len(cov)
    units_in = len([r for r in cov if r["status"] in ("responded", "MULTIPLE")])
    units_out = [r["unit"] for r in cov
                 if r["status"] == "NO RESPONSE" and r["unit"] != "Other"]
    n_products = len(master)
    n_athlete = len([r for r in master if r["athlete_data_likely"] == "Y"])
    n_single = len([r for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) == 1])
    n_mentions = len(long)

    d = BaylorDoc(TITLE, deck=DECK, status=STATUS)

    d.meta([
        ["Status", "**Interim** — collection stays open to the department "
                   "soft deadline of 29 September 2026"],
        ["Date", "29 August 2026"],
        ["Source", "Microsoft Forms — Quick Inventory (5 questions), "
                   "export of 29 August 2026"],
        ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics"],
        ["Companion", "Athletics Technology Inventory — Executive Summary "
                      "(one page)"],
    ])

    d.callout(
        "Two deadlines, not one",
        "29 August was Applied Performance's own deadline. The all-staff "
        "meeting on 24 August set a department-wide soft deadline of "
        "**29 September**, with unit leaders assigning staff to complete the "
        "survey. Every figure in this document is an interim read at the "
        "earlier date, and the units still to respond have a month to run.")

    # --- 1 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("At a glance — where the inventory stands")
    d.table(
        ["Measure", "Figure", "Note"],
        [["Submissions to date", n_resp,
          "36 listed technology; one was a new hire awaiting equipment"],
         ["Units responding", "{} of {}".format(units_in, units_total),
          "Interim — five units still outstanding, one month to run"],
         ["Distinct products", n_products,
          "Resolved from {} separate mentions".format(n_mentions)],
         ["Products touching athlete data", n_athlete,
          "{}% of the estate, by category — a screening list, not a "
          "confirmed count".format(round(100 * n_athlete / n_products))],
         ["Products used by a single unit", n_single,
          "{}% of the estate".format(round(100 * n_single / n_products))]],
        widths=[2.0, 0.9, 3.8], numeric_cols=(1,))

    # --- 2 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Coverage — who has responded")
    d.para("Twenty-seven of thirty-three units have responded so far. Five are "
           "still outstanding, and one of them holds the contract records.")

    d.subhead("Still outstanding")
    d.para("  ·  ".join("**{}**".format(u) for u in units_out), space_after=4)
    d.para("The Business Office is the one worth a direct ask. It holds the "
           "contract records this inventory is designed to be read against.")

    d.subhead("Units that submitted more than once")
    multi = [(r["unit"], r["responses"]) for r in cov if r["status"] == "MULTIPLE"]
    d.para(", ".join("{} ({})".format(u, n) for u, n in multi) + ".",
           space_after=4)
    d.para("These are different people describing different slices of the same "
           "unit. They are kept and tagged rather than merged.")

    d.subhead("The unit list differs from the original form spec")
    d.para("The live Microsoft Form offers units the written spec does not, and "
           "spells two of them differently — which is why Track & Field / Cross "
           "Country and Acrobatics & Tumbling initially appeared as "
           "non-responses. Those spellings are reconciled here. The working "
           "list is {} units and is worth confirming against the live form."
           .format(units_total))

    d.page_break()

    # --- 3 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Coverage detail — response count by unit")
    rows = []
    for r in cov:
        n = int(r["responses"])
        label = ("Not yet in" if n == 0 else
                 "Responded" if n == 1 else "{} people".format(n))
        rows.append([r["unit"], n, label])
    d.table(["Unit", "Responses", "Status"], rows,
            widths=[3.4, 1.0, 2.3], numeric_cols=(1,))

    d.page_break()

    # --- 4 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("The estate — three quarters of it sits with one unit")
    d.para("{} of {} products were named by a single unit. That long tail — not "
           "the vendor overlap — is the finding. It is the population no "
           "central process currently sees.".format(n_single, n_products))
    d.para("It includes AI tools adopted locally (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, "
           "Microsoft Copilot), a scatter of productivity apps (Notion, Asana, "
           "Todoist, Padlet, Sling, GroupMe, WhatsApp, TeamUp), and one-off "
           "athlete-facing systems (Nix Biosensors, Calera CORE, Boost "
           "Treadmills, C3 Logix, XO Armor, Hologic DXA).")

    d.subhead("Distinct products by category")
    cats = {}
    for r in master:
        cats[r["category"]] = cats.get(r["category"], 0) + 1
    d.table(["Category", "Products"],
            [[PRETTY.get(k, k.capitalize()), v]
             for k, v in sorted(cats.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])],
            widths=[3.0, 1.0], numeric_cols=(1,))

    d.subhead("Products used by three or more units")
    d.table(["Product", "Units", "Category"],
            [[r["canonical"], int(r["unit_count"]),
              PRETTY.get(r["category"], r["category"].capitalize())]
             for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) >= 3],
            widths=[2.6, 0.9, 2.2], numeric_cols=(1,))
    d.para("**Teamworks, at twelve units, is the only thing close to a "
           "department-wide system.** Everything below it is departmental at "
           "best.", space_before=3)

    # --- 5 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Overlap — four vendors, one job")
    d.para("The consolidation conversation is now answerable with counts "
           "rather than estimates.")
    d.table(["Job", "Vendors in use"],
            [["Athlete tracking",
              "Catapult (6 units), Kinexon (3), Polar (1); Firstbeat arriving"],
             ["Force & speed testing", "VALD (6), Perch (3), GymAware, TMG"],
             ["Athlete management",
              "Teamworks (12), Kitman Labs (6), XPS Network"],
             ["Video & analytics",
              "Hudl, DVSport, Synergy, Spiideo, Kinovea and 14 more"]],
            widths=[1.9, 4.8])

    d.page_break()

    # --- 6 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Open items — seven products retired, no recorded disposition")
    d.para("Every retirement in the last twelve months left athlete data "
           "somewhere. The short form did not ask where, so the answer is "
           "simply not captured anywhere yet. Confirming what each vendor "
           "retained is the most concrete, closeable action in this dataset.")
    d.table(["Unit", "Product", "Vendor retention"],
            [[r["unit"], r["canonical"], "Not asked"] for r in stopped],
            widths=[2.3, 2.3, 2.1])

    d.subhead("Polar is retired by two units and still running in a third")
    d.para("Athletics Performance and Basketball (W) both stopped using Polar "
           "Team Pro. Basketball (M) lists Polar as currently in use. Surfacing "
           "that automatically, and confirming what a vendor retains when a "
           "unit stops using a product, are two capabilities the framework "
           "would add.")

    d.subhead("Coming online")
    d.bullets([
        "**Softball** — Trackman, about to be installed.",
        "**Athletics Performance** — Firstbeat, purchased, not yet in use.",
    ])
    d.para("Neither can be confirmed against a documented vetting step, "
           "because the short form did not ask.")

    # --- 7 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Signal — one unit answered the underlying question unprompted")
    d.quote("Everything we have has gone through ITS approval, so they have "
            "the list already.")
    d.para("Broadcast and Big Screens, who then listed thirteen vendors: "
           "Ross Video, Evertz, Grass Valley, Calrec, Adder, EditShare, "
           "Riedel, Daktronics, ANC, Haivision, Vyvx, LTN and Switch.")
    d.para("That list is worth checking against the ITS IDEA form history. If "
           "it matches, it is a working baseline for what full compliance "
           "looks like in practice.")

    # --- 8 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Limits — what this data cannot answer")
    d.para("The short form asked five questions. Four things the framework "
           "needs were not among them.")
    d.bullets([
        "**Does it involve student-athlete information, and what kind?** The "
        "{}-product figure is a category inference, not a respondent answer. "
        "Treat it as a screening list.".format(n_athlete),
        "**How is it paid for, and when does the contract end?** Not asked, so "
        "no cross-check against Business Office records is possible from this "
        "data alone.",
        "**Did it go through the ITS IDEA form?** Not asked, so the bypass "
        "rate remains an estimate rather than a measured number.",
        "**Does a vendor still hold data from a discontinued product?** Not "
        "asked. Seven retirements, no dispositions recorded.",
    ])
    d.para("The seventeen-question detailed form was written to close exactly "
           "these four gaps. It has not run yet.")

    d.page_break()

    # --- 9 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Next — recommended steps")
    d.numbered([
        "**Follow up with five units before 29 September.** Golf (M), "
        "Tennis (M), Tennis (W), Volleyball and the Business Office.",
        "**Close the Polar loop.** Two units retired it, a third still runs "
        "it, and what the vendor retained is not recorded. Small, concrete, "
        "demonstrable.",
        "**Run the detailed form as a targeted second pass.** Aimed at the {} "
        "athlete-data candidates this analysis identifies, rather than at all "
        "{} products or at every unit again.".format(n_athlete, n_products),
        "**Ask ITS for the IDEA form history and compare.** That produces the "
        "bypass number from two independent sources instead of a survey "
        "question.",
        "**Decide on the long tail.** {} single-unit products is a policy "
        "question rather than a data question, and it is the one this exercise "
        "exists to raise.".format(n_single),
    ])

    # --- 10 ----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Method — how to read these numbers")
    d.para("Free-text answers were parsed mechanically. Every decision about "
           "whether two strings name the same product is written down and "
           "reversible, and unrecognised names are held for review rather than "
           "assigned to a guess.")

    d.subhead("Judgement calls worth confirming")
    d.bullets([
        "**Hudl** — “HUDL Statsbomb”, “HUDL WyScout” and “HUDL Focus” merged. "
        "Same vendor, three products. This is why Soccer appears as both using "
        "and having stopped Hudl.",
        "**Whistle** — one unit wrote “Whistle (DataViz)”, others wrote bare "
        "“DataViz”. Assumed to be the same product.",
        "**Teamworks** — “TW Nutrition” and “Teamworks Hub” folded in as "
        "modules.",
        "**6-4-3 Charts** — Baseball's “643 Charts” and Softball's “6-4-3” "
        "merged.",
        "**Red Card** — the student-athlete meal-money stipend. It carries "
        "athlete identity and transaction records, so it is counted as athlete "
        "data despite not being a performance system.",
        "**Evertz** — the broadcast answer was one run-on list. Only two items "
        "read as Evertz; the rest map to their own vendors.",
    ])

    d.subhead("Names still to be identified")
    if unmapped:
        d.table(["Named", "By"],
                [[r["raw_item"], r["unit"]] for r in unmapped],
                widths=[2.4, 2.6])
        d.para("Out of {} raw mentions, these are the only names that could "
               "not be resolved to a known product."
               .format(n_mentions + 14), space_before=2)
    else:
        d.para("None outstanding.")

    d.small("Every figure in this document regenerates from the raw export. "
            "Respondent names and email addresses remain in the source file "
            "and appear nowhere in this report.")

    os.makedirs(DELIV, exist_ok=True)
    docx_path = d.save(os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".docx"))
    print("wrote", docx_path)
    print("units {}/{} · products {} · athlete-data {} · single-unit {}"
          .format(units_in, units_total, n_products, n_athlete, n_single))

    pdf_path = os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".pdf")
    n = word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path)
    if n is None:
        print("[warn] Word did not answer, so no PDF was exported and the .pdf "
              "beside this file is stale. Open Microsoft Word and re-run.")
    else:
        print("wrote", pdf_path, "(from Word) ->", n, "page(s)")


def word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path):
    """Export the PDF from Word so it matches the .docx exactly.

    Word blocks on an invisible dialog when the app is not already open, so
    this is best-effort: None means the PDF was not refreshed.
    """
    script = '''
    tell application "Microsoft Word"
      open POSIX file "{docx}"
      set d to active document
      set n to (compute statistics d statistic statistic pages)
      save as d file name POSIX file "{pdf}" file format format PDF
      close d saving no
      return n
    end tell
    '''.format(docx=docx_path, pdf=pdf_path)
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["osascript", "-e", script],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=180)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return None
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return None
    try:
        return int(r.stdout.strip())
    except ValueError:
        return None


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

DELIV = os.path.join(ROOT, "deliverables")
STEM = "Tech_Inventory_FINDINGS_ER_2026-08-29"

TITLE = "Athletics Technology Inventory"
DECK = ("Thirty-seven submissions across the department. The finding is not "
        "that there is too much technology — it is that almost none of it is "
        "shared.")
STATUS = "Interim — collection open to 29 September 2026"

PRETTY = {"video-analytics": "Video & analytics", "comms-media": "Comms & media",
          "office-general": "Office general", "equipment-ops": "Equipment ops",
          "athlete-management": "Athlete management", "ai-general": "AI tools",
          "food-travel": "Food & travel", "social-media": "Social media",
          "athlete-stipend": "Athlete stipend", "uncategorised": "Unidentified"}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# data
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load():
    def rd(name):
        with open(os.path.join(CLEAN, name), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return list(csv.DictReader(f))

    master = [r for r in rd("tech_master.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    long = [r for r in rd("tech_inventory_long.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    return (master, long, rd("coverage.csv"), rd("stopped_using.csv"),
            rd("unmapped_review.csv"))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main():
    master, long, cov, stopped, unmapped = load()

    n_resp = len({r["response_id"] for r in long}) + 1   # + the prose response
    units_total = len(cov)
    units_in = len([r for r in cov if r["status"] in ("responded", "MULTIPLE")])
    units_out = [r["unit"] for r in cov
                 if r["status"] == "NO RESPONSE" and r["unit"] != "Other"]
    n_products = len(master)
    n_athlete = len([r for r in master if r["athlete_data_likely"] == "Y"])
    n_single = len([r for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) == 1])
    n_mentions = len(long)

    d = BaylorDoc(TITLE, deck=DECK, status=STATUS)

    d.meta([
        ["Status", "**Interim** — collection stays open to the department "
                   "soft deadline of 29 September 2026"],
        ["Date", "29 August 2026"],
        ["Source", "Microsoft Forms — Quick Inventory (5 questions), "
                   "export of 29 August 2026"],
        ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics"],
        ["Companion", "Athletics Technology Inventory — Executive Summary "
                      "(one page)"],
    ])

    d.callout(
        "Two deadlines, not one",
        "29 August was Applied Performance's own deadline. The all-staff "
        "meeting on 24 August set a department-wide soft deadline of "
        "**29 September**, with unit leaders assigning staff to complete the "
        "survey. Every figure in this document is an interim read at the "
        "earlier date, and the units still to respond have a month to run.")

    # --- 1 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("At a glance — where the inventory stands")
    d.table(
        ["Measure", "Figure", "Note"],
        [["Submissions to date", n_resp,
          "36 listed technology; one was a new hire awaiting equipment"],
         ["Units responding", "{} of {}".format(units_in, units_total),
          "Interim — five units still outstanding, one month to run"],
         ["Distinct products", n_products,
          "Resolved from {} separate mentions".format(n_mentions)],
         ["Products touching athlete data", n_athlete,
          "{}% of the estate, by category — a screening list, not a "
          "confirmed count".format(round(100 * n_athlete / n_products))],
         ["Products used by a single unit", n_single,
          "{}% of the estate".format(round(100 * n_single / n_products))]],
        widths=[2.0, 0.9, 3.8], numeric_cols=(1,))

    # --- 2 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Coverage — who has responded")
    d.para("Twenty-seven of thirty-three units have responded so far. Five are "
           "still outstanding, and one of them holds the contract records.")

    d.subhead("Still outstanding")
    d.para("  ·  ".join("**{}**".format(u) for u in units_out), space_after=4)
    d.para("The Business Office is the one worth a direct ask. It holds the "
           "contract records this inventory is designed to be read against.")

    d.subhead("Units that submitted more than once")
    multi = [(r["unit"], r["responses"]) for r in cov if r["status"] == "MULTIPLE"]
    d.para(", ".join("{} ({})".format(u, n) for u, n in multi) + ".",
           space_after=4)
    d.para("These are different people describing different slices of the same "
           "unit. They are kept and tagged rather than merged.")

    d.subhead("The unit list differs from the original form spec")
    d.para("The live Microsoft Form offers units the written spec does not, and "
           "spells two of them differently — which is why Track & Field / Cross "
           "Country and Acrobatics & Tumbling initially appeared as "
           "non-responses. Those spellings are reconciled here. The working "
           "list is {} units and is worth confirming against the live form."
           .format(units_total))

    d.page_break()

    # --- 3 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Coverage detail — response count by unit")
    rows = []
    for r in cov:
        n = int(r["responses"])
        label = ("Not yet in" if n == 0 else
                 "Responded" if n == 1 else "{} people".format(n))
        rows.append([r["unit"], n, label])
    d.table(["Unit", "Responses", "Status"], rows,
            widths=[3.4, 1.0, 2.3], numeric_cols=(1,))

    d.page_break()

    # --- 4 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("The estate — three quarters of it sits with one unit")
    d.para("{} of {} products were named by a single unit. That long tail — not "
           "the vendor overlap — is the finding. It is the population no "
           "central process currently sees.".format(n_single, n_products))
    d.para("It includes AI tools adopted locally (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, "
           "Microsoft Copilot), a scatter of productivity apps (Notion, Asana, "
           "Todoist, Padlet, Sling, GroupMe, WhatsApp, TeamUp), and one-off "
           "athlete-facing systems (Nix Biosensors, Calera CORE, Boost "
           "Treadmills, C3 Logix, XO Armor, Hologic DXA).")

    d.subhead("Distinct products by category")
    cats = {}
    for r in master:
        cats[r["category"]] = cats.get(r["category"], 0) + 1
    d.table(["Category", "Products"],
            [[PRETTY.get(k, k.capitalize()), v]
             for k, v in sorted(cats.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])],
            widths=[3.0, 1.0], numeric_cols=(1,))

    d.subhead("Products used by three or more units")
    d.table(["Product", "Units", "Category"],
            [[r["canonical"], int(r["unit_count"]),
              PRETTY.get(r["category"], r["category"].capitalize())]
             for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) >= 3],
            widths=[2.6, 0.9, 2.2], numeric_cols=(1,))
    d.para("**Teamworks, at twelve units, is the only thing close to a "
           "department-wide system.** Everything below it is departmental at "
           "best.", space_before=3)

    # --- 5 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Overlap — four vendors, one job")
    d.para("The consolidation conversation is now answerable with counts "
           "rather than estimates.")
    d.table(["Job", "Vendors in use"],
            [["Athlete tracking",
              "Catapult (6 units), Kinexon (3), Polar (1); Firstbeat arriving"],
             ["Force & speed testing", "VALD (6), Perch (3), GymAware, TMG"],
             ["Athlete management",
              "Teamworks (12), Kitman Labs (6), XPS Network"],
             ["Video & analytics",
              "Hudl, DVSport, Synergy, Spiideo, Kinovea and 14 more"]],
            widths=[1.9, 4.8])

    d.page_break()

    # --- 6 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Open items — seven products retired, no recorded disposition")
    d.para("Every retirement in the last twelve months left athlete data "
           "somewhere. The short form did not ask where, so the answer is "
           "simply not captured anywhere yet. Confirming what each vendor "
           "retained is the most concrete, closeable action in this dataset.")
    d.table(["Unit", "Product", "Vendor retention"],
            [[r["unit"], r["canonical"], "Not asked"] for r in stopped],
            widths=[2.3, 2.3, 2.1])

    d.subhead("Polar is retired by two units and still running in a third")
    d.para("Athletics Performance and Basketball (W) both stopped using Polar "
           "Team Pro. Basketball (M) lists Polar as currently in use. Surfacing "
           "that automatically, and confirming what a vendor retains when a "
           "unit stops using a product, are two capabilities the framework "
           "would add.")

    d.subhead("Coming online")
    d.bullets([
        "**Softball** — Trackman, about to be installed.",
        "**Athletics Performance** — Firstbeat, purchased, not yet in use.",
    ])
    d.para("Neither can be confirmed against a documented vetting step, "
           "because the short form did not ask.")

    # --- 7 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Signal — one unit answered the underlying question unprompted")
    d.quote("Everything we have has gone through ITS approval, so they have "
            "the list already.")
    d.para("Broadcast and Big Screens, who then listed thirteen vendors: "
           "Ross Video, Evertz, Grass Valley, Calrec, Adder, EditShare, "
           "Riedel, Daktronics, ANC, Haivision, Vyvx, LTN and Switch.")
    d.para("That list is worth checking against the ITS IDEA form history. If "
           "it matches, it is a working baseline for what full compliance "
           "looks like in practice.")

    # --- 8 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Limits — what this data cannot answer")
    d.para("The short form asked five questions. Four things the framework "
           "needs were not among them.")
    d.bullets([
        "**Does it involve student-athlete information, and what kind?** The "
        "{}-product figure is a category inference, not a respondent answer. "
        "Treat it as a screening list.".format(n_athlete),
        "**How is it paid for, and when does the contract end?** Not asked, so "
        "no cross-check against Business Office records is possible from this "
        "data alone.",
        "**Did it go through the ITS IDEA form?** Not asked, so the bypass "
        "rate remains an estimate rather than a measured number.",
        "**Does a vendor still hold data from a discontinued product?** Not "
        "asked. Seven retirements, no dispositions recorded.",
    ])
    d.para("The seventeen-question detailed form was written to close exactly "
           "these four gaps. It has not run yet.")

    d.page_break()

    # --- 9 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Next — recommended steps")
    d.numbered([
        "**Follow up with five units before 29 September.** Golf (M), "
        "Tennis (M), Tennis (W), Volleyball and the Business Office.",
        "**Close the Polar loop.** Two units retired it, a third still runs "
        "it, and what the vendor retained is not recorded. Small, concrete, "
        "demonstrable.",
        "**Run the detailed form as a targeted second pass.** Aimed at the {} "
        "athlete-data candidates this analysis identifies, rather than at all "
        "{} products or at every unit again.".format(n_athlete, n_products),
        "**Ask ITS for the IDEA form history and compare.** That produces the "
        "bypass number from two independent sources instead of a survey "
        "question.",
        "**Decide on the long tail.** {} single-unit products is a policy "
        "question rather than a data question, and it is the one this exercise "
        "exists to raise.".format(n_single),
    ])

    # --- 10 ----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Method — how to read these numbers")
    d.para("Free-text answers were parsed mechanically. Every decision about "
           "whether two strings name the same product is written down and "
           "reversible, and unrecognised names are held for review rather than "
           "assigned to a guess.")

    d.subhead("Judgement calls worth confirming")
    d.bullets([
        "**Hudl** — “HUDL Statsbomb”, “HUDL WyScout” and “HUDL Focus” merged. "
        "Same vendor, three products. This is why Soccer appears as both using "
        "and having stopped Hudl.",
        "**Whistle** — one unit wrote “Whistle (DataViz)”, others wrote bare "
        "“DataViz”. Assumed to be the same product.",
        "**Teamworks** — “TW Nutrition” and “Teamworks Hub” folded in as "
        "modules.",
        "**6-4-3 Charts** — Baseball's “643 Charts” and Softball's “6-4-3” "
        "merged.",
        "**Red Card** — the student-athlete meal-money stipend. It carries "
        "athlete identity and transaction records, so it is counted as athlete "
        "data despite not being a performance system.",
        "**Evertz** — the broadcast answer was one run-on list. Only two items "
        "read as Evertz; the rest map to their own vendors.",
    ])

    d.subhead("Names still to be identified")
    if unmapped:
        d.table(["Named", "By"],
                [[r["raw_item"], r["unit"]] for r in unmapped],
                widths=[2.4, 2.6])
        d.para("Out of {} raw mentions, these are the only names that could "
               "not be resolved to a known product."
               .format(n_mentions + 14), space_before=2)
    else:
        d.para("None outstanding.")

    d.small("Every figure in this document regenerates from the raw export. "
            "Respondent names and email addresses remain in the source file "
            "and appear nowhere in this report.")

    os.makedirs(DELIV, exist_ok=True)
    docx_path = d.save(os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".docx"))
    print("wrote", docx_path)
    print("units {}/{} · products {} · athlete-data {} · single-unit {}"
          .format(units_in, units_total, n_products, n_athlete, n_single))

    pdf_path = os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".pdf")
    n = word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path)
    if n is None:
        print("[warn] Word did not answer, so no PDF was exported and the .pdf "
              "beside this file is stale. Open Microsoft Word and re-run.")
    else:
        print("wrote", pdf_path, "(from Word) ->", n, "page(s)")


def word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path):
    """Export the PDF from Word so it matches the .docx exactly.

    Word blocks on an invisible dialog when the app is not already open, so
    this is best-effort: None means the PDF was not refreshed.
    """
    script = '''
    tell application "Microsoft Word"
      open POSIX file "{docx}"
      set d to active document
      set n to (compute statistics d statistic statistic pages)
      save as d file name POSIX file "{pdf}" file format format PDF
      close d saving no
      return n
    end tell
    '''.format(docx=docx_path, pdf=pdf_path)
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["osascript", "-e", script],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=180)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return None
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return None
    try:
        return int(r.stdout.strip())
    except ValueError:
        return None


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

input.content:
# Baylor Doc Style

The house look for Baylor Athletics Word documents, defined once.

`baylor_docstyle.py` is a single module. Document builders import it instead of
setting their own fonts, colours and spacing, so every document comes out
looking like the same department wrote it.

## Where the style comes from

Every measurement in the module was read out of:

```
~/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/deliverables/
    Software_and_Technology_Management_Framework_DRAFT.docx
```

Eric chose that document as the house look on 2026-08-30. Nothing in the module
is invented. **If the module and that document ever disagree, the document
wins** — re-measure it rather than adjusting to taste.

## Use

```python
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style")
from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc

d = BaylorDoc("Athletics Technology Inventory",
              deck="What the department runs, and who runs it.",
              status="Interim — collection open to 29 September 2026")

d.meta([["Status", "Interim"], ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance"]])
d.callout("Two deadlines, not one", "29 August was our own deadline...")
d.section("Coverage — who has responded")     # numbered automatically
d.subhead("Still outstanding")
d.para("Five units have yet to respond.")
d.bullets(["**Softball** — Trackman, about to be installed."])
d.numbered(["**Follow up with five units.** Golf (M), Tennis (M)..."])
d.quote("Everything we have has gone through ITS approval.")
d.table(["Unit", "Responses"], [["Football", 3]], numeric_cols=(1,))
d.note("A caveat, in small italic grey.")
d.small("A caption under a table.")
d.save("out.docx")
```

`**double asterisks**` mark inline bold in every text argument.

Section numbers are handed out in order, so inserting a section never means
renumbering the ones after it.

## What the style is

| Element | Setting |
|---|---|
| Page | Letter, margins 0.80in top/bottom, 0.90in left/right |
| Body | Calibri 10.5pt, 6pt after, line spacing 1.079 |
| Eyebrow | 9pt bold, gold `#B8860B` |
| Title | 19pt bold, Baylor green `#154734` |
| Deck | 11pt italic, grey `#595959` |
| Meta block | borderless label/value, 9pt |
| Callout | cream `#FFF4DA` box, 9.5pt, green heading |
| Section | numbered, 13pt bold green, green rule under |
| Subhead | 11.5pt bold green |
| Table | green header band, white header text, 9.5pt body |
| Footer | centred 7.5pt grey — title, status, "Baylor Athletics", page number |
| Header | none |

## Three things not to change

**Calibri, everywhere.** The exemplar sets no font on any run, so every size
inherits Normal. Calibri ships with Office, which is why the document survives
being emailed. Baylor's licensed faces are in `~/DEV/Baylor_Fonts`, but a
document set in them falls back to something else on any machine that lacks
them.

**No running header.** The exemplar has an empty header and carries the
document's status in the meta block and the footer instead. That still puts the
status on every page, which is the constraint that matters.

**No hand-placed page breaks.** Headings carry keep-with-next, so Word breaks
the document itself. A hand-placed break is correct only until the content above
it changes length, and then it leaves a half-empty page.

## Exporting to PDF

Open Microsoft Word first, then export the PDF from the `.docx` so the two files
match. Word blocks on a dialog the caller cannot see when the app is not already
running. See `word_pdf()` in
`~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis/scripts/build_docx.py` for the working call.

## Who uses it

- `~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis/scripts/build_docx.py` — findings report
- `~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis/scripts/build_exec_summary.py` — one-page summary
